Other popular attack techniques that can be traced back to his research include web cache poisoning, the single-packet attack, server-side template injection, and password reset poisoning. He's also the designer behind many of the topics and labs that make up the Web Security Academy. You can reach him on X, formerly known as Twitter, at @albinowax.

He has led the design and development of anti-malware scanning solutions, reverse-engineered complex malware and cryptographic libraries, directed threat intelligence teams investigating nation-state hackers, performed digital forensics/incident response for high-profile breaches, and conducted penetration testing and security audits for large organizations. Tom was among the first security researchers to investigate real-world attacks against deep learning systems and has been actively developing offensive tooling and defensive countermeasures in the AI space since 2019. Additionally, Tom has been published dozens of times, co-authored a book on threat intelligence, and presented at several industry conferences.

43758.title: Security Researcher
43758.bio: Thijs Alkemade (@xnyhps) works at the security research division of Computest, Sector 7. This division is responsible for advanced security research on commonly used systems and environments. Thijs has won the famous Pwn2Own competition twice, by demonstrating a zero-day attack against Zoom at Pwn2Own Vancouver 2021 and by demonstrating multiple exploits in ICS systems at Pwn2Own Miami 2022. In previous research, he demonstrated several attacks against the macOS and iOS operating systems. He has a background in both mathematics and computer science, which gives him a lot of experience with cryptography and programming language theory.

48194.title: Security Researcher
48194.bio:
Khaled Nassar works at the security research division of Computest Security. This division is responsible for advanced security research on commonly used systems and environments.

Khaled has participated in Pwn2Own Automotive 2024 in Tokyo, demonstrating exploits in various EV chargers. In 2021 and 2022, he jailbroke devices built upon the Tuya IoT platform. He has a background in computer science and has worn many hats in tech alongside security, including development and operations.

40579.title: CTO
40579.bio: Michael Bargury is a security researcher passionate about all things related to cloud, SaaS and low-code security, and spends his time finding ways they could go wrong. He is the Co-Founder and CTO of Zenity, where he helps companies secure their low-code/no-code apps. In the past, he headed security product efforts at Azure focused on IoT, APIs and IaC. He also leads the OWASP No-Code/Low-Code Top 10 project and writes about it on DarkReading. Michael is a regular speaker at Black Hat, DEFCON, OWASP and BSides. You can find his DarkReading column at https://www.darkreading.com/author/michael-bargury and personal blog at https://mbgsec.com/﻿

49083.title: Senior Security Researcher
49083.bio: Avishai Efrati is a Senior Security Researcher at Zenity. Avishai is a Certified ethical hacker & security researcher and data engineer. Avishai is experienced with cloud security, advanced SQL/ETL pipelines; relational DBs (SQL Server/MySQL) & big data technologies (ElasticSearch/Spark); security data analysis; web application hacking/OSInt/reconnaissance; anti-bot protection & botting; PowerShell; Python; Bash; Linux/Windows OS; Azure Databricks & PySpark optimization; JavasScript/TypeScript; botting/web automation; the AWS/Azure cloud platforms; Blockchain/Ethereum/Solidity; and different aspects of ethical hacking, bug bounties and OWASP vulnerabilities.

44483.title: Vulnerability Researcher
44483.bio: Noam Moshe is a vulnerability researcher at Claroty Team82. Noam specializes in vulnerability research, web applications pentesting, malware analysis, network forensics and ICS/SCADA security. In addition, Noam presented in well-known Hacking conferences like Black Hat and Defcon, as well as winning Master of Pwn at Pwn2Own Miami 2023.

33061.title: Computer Security Researcher
33061.bio: Zisis Sialveras, a computer security researcher from Greece, is currently employed at CENSUS S.A. His professional portfolio encompasses a diverse array of tasks including vulnerability research, reverse engineering, source code auditing, and exploit development. Previously, he delved into experimenting with knowledge-based fuzzers and breaking hypervisors. However, his recent endeavors have steered towards exploring the intricacies of browser security.

46819.title: Security Researcher
46819.bio: Tom Dohrmann is a Software Developer and Security Researcher. His main focuses are embedded systems, OS security, and reverse engineering.

32558.title: Team Lead and Security Engineer
32558.bio: Natalie Silvanovich leads Google Project Zero's North American team. Her current research focus is messaging applications and video conferencing. Previously, she worked in mobile security on the Android Security Team at Google and as a team lead of the Security Research Group at BlackBerry, where her work included finding security issues in mobile software and improving the security of mobile platforms. Outside of work, Natalie enjoys applying her hacking and reverse engineering skills to unusual targets and has spoken at several conferences on the subject of Tamagotchi hacking.

48215.title: Research Fellow
48215.bio: Fredrik Heiding is a research fellow in computer science at Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences. He researches how to mitigate AI-enabled cyberattacks via technical innovations, organizational strategies, and national security policies. Fredrik works with the World Economic Forum's Cybercrime Center to improve global and domestic cybersecurity standards of AI-based cyber defense. He is a teaching fellow for the Generative AI for Business Leaders course at the Harvard Business School and leads the cybersecurity division of the Harvard AI Safety Student Team (HAISST). His technical research serves as a benchmark for evaluating the offensive capabilities of frontier AI models. In early 2022, Fredrik got media attention for hacking the King of Sweden and the Swedish European Commissioner. His previous study on AI-enabled spear phishing attacks was presented at Black Hat 2023, and he co-hosted a disinformation village at Defcon 2023. You can follow Fredrik on X @fredheiding

48567.title: Independet
48567.bio: Alex O'Neill is a national security researcher who studies emerging technology, cyber threats, and illicit finance. His current work focuses on North Korea's financially motivated cyber operations and ties to the Russian-speaking cybercriminal ecosystem. Until 2023, Alex was an Associate at the Harvard Kennedy School's Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs as well as Coordinator of the Belfer Center's Korea Project, where he co-founded and led for three years the North Korea Cyber Working Group (NK CWG). He previously worked at the Belfer Center's Project on Managing the Atom. Alex regularly presents his research to academic, industry, and government audiences and has delivered briefings on North Korean cyber activities to the U.S. State Department, Treasury Department, and intelligence agencies. His prior research includes "Upholding North Korea Sanctions in the Age of Decentralised Finance" and "Cybercriminal Statecraft: North Korean Hackers' Ties to the Global Underground." Alex received an MSc in Russian and East European Studies from the University of Oxford and a BA with distinction in History from Yale University.

48568.title: Research Assistant
48568.bio: Lachlan Price, before working with the National Cybersecurity Strategies Evaluating project, was a Digital Consultant at McKinsey and Company Australia, where he worked on developing the Australian 2023-2030 Cybersecurity Strategy. Lachlan also has extensive experience supporting public sector cybersecurity projects, and is currently a dual Master in Public Policy and Master of Business Administration candidate at the Harvard Kennedy School and MIT Sloan School of Management.

48569.title: Senior Lecturer in Public Policy
48569.bio: The Honorable Eric Rosenbach is a Senior Lecturer at the Harvard Kennedy School and is the Director of the Defense, Emerging Technology, and Strategy Program at the Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs.  He previously co-led the Belfer Center with former Secretary of Defense Ash Carter.  Rosenbach currently serves on the Secretary of State's International Security Advisory Board and on the Secretary of Defense's Defense Business Board. Rosenbach teaches graduate courses in policy development, strategy execution, and international security. He also teaches two online courses for HarvardX on managing cyber risk and public sector strategy execution. He previously held several senior-level appointee jobs in government.  As the Chief of Staff to the Secretary of Defense from 2015-2017, Rosenbach was one of the senior-most leaders in the Department of Defense.  He served as Secretary Ash Carter's closest strategic advisor on key policy initiatives, such as the war to defeat ISIS, the "rebalance" to Asia, and the effort to check Russian aggression. Rosenbach also led the Department's efforts to improve innovation by forging and managing key initiatives such as the Defense Digital Service and the Defense Innovation Unit. Before serving as Chief of Staff, Rosenbach was the Senate-confirmed Assistant Secretary of Defense for Global Security and Homeland Defense.  His diverse portfolio as Assistant Secretary included cyber, space, countering the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, antiterrorism, continuity of government, and defense support to civil authorities. Earlier, Rosenbach served as Deputy Assistant Secretary for Cyber Policy. Rosenbach previously served as national security advisor for then-Senator Chuck Hagel and as a professional staff member on the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, where he led oversight of Intelligence Community counterterrorism programs.   A former Army intelligence officer and commander of a telecommunications intelligence unit, Rosenbach led a team that worked closely with the NSA to provide strategic intelligence in direct support of commanders in Bosnia and Kosovo. He has published widely and authored several books, including "Confronting Cyber Risk: An Embedded Endurance Strategy".  The LA Times called his book "Find, Fix, Finish", co-authored with Aki Peritz, "an important volume in the secret history of a nasty war."

38299.title: Senior Director of Research
38299.bio:
Nathan Hamiel is Senior Director of Research at Kudelski Security where he leads the fundamental and applied research team. Part of the Innovation group working to define the future of products and services for the company, his team focuses on privacy, advanced cryptography, emerging technologies, and special projects. He is also responsible for the research function at the company, connecting the dots between the various business units and focusing on collaboration both internal and external to the company. For over 20 years, he has helped customers worldwide solve complex security challenges and accelerate innovation.
 
Nathan spends his time focusing on emerging and disruptive technologies and their intersection with information security. This research includes new approaches to difficult security problems and the safety, security, and privacy of artificial intelligence. He is a proponent of agility and simplification and their application in solving security challenges. Nathan is a regular public speaker and has presented his research at global security events, including Black Hat, DEF CON, HOPE, ShmooCon, SecTor, ToorCon, and many others. He is also a veteran member of the Black Hat review board, where he serves as the track lead for the AI, ML, and Data Science track.

41682.title: Corporate Vice President and Deputy CISO
41682.bio:
Ann Johnson is Corporate Vice President and Deputy CISO at Microsoft. In this role, Ann drives all external engagement for the Microsoft Office of the CISO, and leads security risk management, standards, and governance for the company's Sales and Partner organization. She is a long tenured, recognized thought leader on cybersecurity and a sought-after global speaker and digital author specializing in cyber resilience, online fraud, cyberattacks, compliance, and security.

Ann challenges traditional schools of thought and cyber-norms–from the way the tech industry tackles cyber threats to the language it uses to communicate–and encourages the industry to get outside its comfort zones and expand how it addresses the evolving threat landscape with the power of technology and people. As a global cybersecurity leader and strategist, she is looking ahead at how today's cybersecurity investments will impact tomorrow's cybersecurity reality.

Ann currently serves on the Board of Directors of Seattle Humane, N-Able, Human Security, Datavant, and is Member of the Board of Advisors for Cybersecurity Center of Excellence, WA and the Signal Cyber Museum Society. Ann is also the Executive Sponsor of the Microsoft Women in Security Group.

40008.title: Director, Threat Intelligence Strategy
40008.bio:
Sherrod DeGrippo is Director of Threat Intelligence Strategy at Microsoft. She was selected as Cybersecurity woman of the year in 2022 and Cybersecurity PR Spokesperson of the year for 2021.

Previously, she was VP of Threat Research and Detection at Proofpoint, where she led a global team of threat researchers, malware reverse engineers and threat intelligence analysts. Her career in cybersecurity spans 20 years with prior roles including leading Red Team Services at Nexum, senior solutions engineer for Symantec, senior security consultant for Secureworks, and senior network security analyst for the National Nuclear Security Admin.

She is a frequently cited threat intelligence expert in media including televised appearances on the BBC News, and commentary in the Wall Street Journal, Washington Post, CNN, New York Times, and more. Having presented at Black Hat, RSA conference, RMISC, SleuthCon, and others, Sherrod is a well known public speaker, and the host of THE Microsoft Threat Intelligence podcast.

In her personal time, Sherrod spends time with her rescue dog Boris Karloff.

42887.title: CEO & Co-Founder
42887.bio: Danny Jenkins, CEO & Co-Founder of ThreatLocker, a cybersecurity firm providing Zero Trust endpoint security, is a leading cybersecurity expert with over two decades of experience building and securing corporate networks, including roles on red and blue teams. He is dedicated to educating industry professionals about the latest cyber threats and frequently speaks on the topics of ransomware and Zero Trust.

45359.title: Security Researcher
45359.bio: Adnan is a Red Team Security Engineer and Security Researcher who has recently been focusing on supply chain and CI/CD attacks. He has identified, demonstrated, and reported vulnerabilities impacting GitHub repositories belonging to organizations like Microsoft, Nvidia, OpenAI, GitHub, Google, and more. Additionally, he has spoken at conferences such as ShmooCon 2023 and BSides SF 2023.

47583.title: Security Researcher
47583.bio: John Stawinski is an offensive security engineer, vulnerability researcher, and writer, specializing in Red Team operations and CICD security. John established himself as a member of the broader security community in 2023 through a series of CI/CD attacks on prominent open-source repositories. Embracing a nomadic lifestyle, John thrives on adventure sports and welcomes new experiences.

39002.title: Senior Analyst
39002.bio: Sanne Maasakkers works as a senior analyst at Mandiant Intelligence (now part of Google Cloud). After working in offensive security and in the public sector, she now focuses on researching and analyzing digital threats and APT tactics. She presented before on the DEFCON Adversary Village, BSides Las Vegas and the Grace Hopper Celebration for Women in Tech about hacking and threat intelligence. Aside from these professional roles, she coaches the European CTF team (backed by ENISA) for the yearly international championship, leads the EU initiative at the Adversary Village and creates educational content about hacking for the younger generation.

41457.title: Researcher
41457.bio: Gareth Heyes, PortSwigger researcher, is probably best known for smashing the AngularJS sandbox to pieces and creating super-elegant XSS vectors. He is the author of JavaScript for hackers. In his daily life at PortSwigger, Gareth can often be found creating new XSS vectors, and researching new techniques to attack web applications. He has a keen interest in hacking CSS to do wonderful, unexpected things and can often be seen experimenting with 3D pure CSS rooms, games and taking markup languages to the limit on his website. He's also the author of PortSwigger's XSS Cheat Sheet. In his spare time, he loves writing new BApp extensions such as Hackvertor.

33011.title: CTO & Co-Founder
33011.bio: Chris Wysopal is the founder and CTO at Veracode with responsibility for security research, product security and information security. Prior to joining Veracode, Chris worked as a software developer before diving into security research and security consulting. He had security research roles at several companies, including Symantec, @stake and the hacker think tank, L0pht where he was one of the original vulnerability researchers in the 1990s. He has testified on Capitol Hill in the US on the subjects of government computer security and how vulnerabilities are discovered in software. He is also the author of "The Art of Software Security Testing" published by Addison-Wesley.

48077.title: Independent Security Researcher
48077.bio: Qinghe Xie (@Q1ngH3) is a graduate student at the Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences. He focuses on fuzzing and reverse engineering, and is very interested in Windows and Virtualization Security. He was acknowledged by Hex-rays for discovering several vulnerabilities in IDA Pro and was ranked Top #6 on the 2024 Q1 MSRC Windows Security Researcher Leaderboard. His work has been recognized by security conferences such as TyphoonCon.

40306.title: PhD Candidate
40306.bio: Fangming Gu (@afang5472) is a doctoral candidate at the Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences. His focus is on Windows security research and complex software reverse engineering. He also devotes time to building automated bug finding tools. He discovered many Windows vulnerabilities in the past years and was ranked Top #14 on the MSRC Most Valuable Security Researcher list in 2020 and Top #21 in 2021. His work has been recognized by prestigious security conferences such as Usenix Security and Black Hat.

45132.title: Security Researcher
45132.company: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
45132.bio: P1umer is currently a Master in Cyberspace Security at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and a member of the NeSE CTF team. He is mainly engaged in browser and kernel security research. His previous work on WASM compiler of browsers was presented at Black Hat Asia 23.

48662.title: Postdoctoral Researcher
48662.company: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
48662.bio: Qingli Guo is a postdoctoral researcher at the Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences. She earned her doctoral degree from the Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Her research interests include binary program understanding, software security, and hardware security. She has published numerous works in leading security and software engineering conferences such as Usenix Security, ESORICS, and SANER.

44988.title: Senior Security Researcher
44988.bio: Liv Matan is a Senior Security Researcher at Tenable, where he specializes in application and web security. As a bug bounty hunter, Liv has found several vulnerabilities in popular software platforms, such as Azure, Google Cloud, AWS, Facebook, and Gitlab, was recognized as Microsoft's Most Valuable Researcher, and presented at conferences such as DEF CON Cloud Village and fwd:cloudsec. You can follow Liv on X @terminatorlm

38868.title: Security Engineer
38868.bio: Bill Demirkapi is a security researcher for the Microsoft Security Response Center with an intense passion for Windows Internals. His interests include reverse engineering and vulnerability research, ranging from low-level memory corruption to systemic flaws with catastrophic consequences. He started his journey in high school and has since published his work at internationally-recognized conferences like DEF CON and Black Hat USA. In his pursuit to make the world a better place, Bill constantly looks for the next significant vulnerability, following the motto "break anything and everything".

48171.title: VP Security
48171.bio: Cory Michal is an information security professional with over fifteen years of technical and leadership experience. He has worked extensively in building and managing pragmatic information security programs to accomplish strategic organizational objectives, reduce risk and improve security posture. Cory has built and led large high performing teams, published vulnerability research, and worked on the board of security conferences. His work on organizational Red Team engagements and threat modeling has made him well known within the industry.

36968.title: Principal Product Manager, Threat Detection
36968.bio: Brandon Levene has worked in threat research for over a decade, focusing primarily on financially motivated threat actors. He is currently the Principal Product Manager for Threat Detection at AppOmni. He is also an adjunct professor at the Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS), where he developed an original course on Cybercrime and Cybercriminals. He began his career as a security analyst at Dell SecureWorks, and has worked at Salesforce, Palo Alto Networks, Google, and Microsoft. His responsibilities at Google and Chronicle included leading Applied Intelligence, leading significant projects involving threat research and community facilitation. He was also a member of the Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center where he tracked adversaries specializing in ransomware. In 2023, Brandon Levene founded Lightforge Ventures, which specializes in product-led investigations to assist organizations in creating content with security in mind. In his spare time, he is an amateur music producer, voracious reader, and avid gamer (including card games like Magic: The Gathering).

48244.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Threat Research
48244.bio: Ben Pruce is a seasoned cybersecurity professional with over a decade of expertise in threat research. Currently serving as Senior Engineering Manager for Threat Research at AppOmni, they lead a research team producing customer-facing detection rules, specializing in emerging SaaS threats. Prior roles at HashiCorp and Salesforce saw them spearheading initiatives to enhance detection and response capabilities, implementing behavioral detection rules, building automation pipelines, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to bolster security posture.

38395.title: Principal Engineer, Offensive Security Researcher
38395.bio: Arun Kanuparthi is a Sr. Offensive Security Researcher with Intel's Product Assurance and Security group. He leads the offensive security research efforts on Intel's datacenter networking and 5G products. His research interests include hardware and system security, vulnerability root causing and mitigations, hardware security assurance, and formal verification for security. He is the lead contributor of over 75+ entries to MITRE's hardware CWE. He co-organizes the Hack@event hardware hacking competition.

33088.title: Principal Engineer, Offensive Security Research
33088.bio: Hareesh Khattri is a Principal Offensive Security Researcher at Intel. He has over 15 years of offensive security research on multiple Intel product segments such as Servers, clients, cores, modems, etc.

46148.title: Senior Director, Offensive Security Research & Academic Research Engagement
46148.bio:
Jason M. Fung is the Senior Director of Offensive Security Research and Academic Research Engagement at Intel Product Assurance and Security. He oversees emerging threat research of key technologies that power Intel's edge, communication and data center products. He also leads academic and industry collaborations that advance best practices in product security assurance for the semiconductor industry. Recent contributions include the creation of the community-driven Hardware Common Weakness Enumeration (cwe.mitre.org), the industry-first Pre-Si Hardware Capture-the-Flag Competitions (HackAtEvent.org), and the Intel Research Experience for Undergraduates Program focusing on nurturing future security leaders in collaboration with Princeton, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Georgia Tech. He is a founding member of the MITRE CAPEC/CWE Advisory Board.
Over his 25-year tenure at Intel, Jason has held various roles encompassing architecture and performance, verification automation, research and pathfinding, security assurance and consultation, and engineering management. Since 2013, he has served on steering committees and founded the Security tracks for several premier conferences at Intel. He has authored 7 US patents and dozens of publications in peer-reviewed academic, industry and Intel technical conferences. He holds a M.S. degree and two B.S. degrees in Electrical & Computer Engineering and Computer Science from Carnegie Mellon University.

46150.title: Associate Professor
46150.bio: JV Rajendran is an Associate Professor in the Electrical Engineering department at Texas A&M University. He obtained his PhD in Electrical Engineering from New York University.

31702.title: Professor
31702.bio: Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi is a Full Professor of Computer Science at the Technical University of Darmstadt, Germany, where he heads the System Security Lab. Since 2012 Prof. Sadeghi has established a long-term cooperation with Intel. It has already emerged in several Collaborative Research Centers on various topics, such as Secure Computing in Mobile and Embedded Systems, Autonomous and Resilient Systems, and Private AI. Moreover, he also established the Open Lab for Sustainable Security and Safety (OpenS3 Lab) with Huawei in 2019. He received his Ph.D. in Computer Science with a focus on Cryptography from the University of Saarland, Germany. Before academia, he worked for several years in the Research and Development of the Telecommunications industry, amongst others, Ericsson. He has been leading and involved in many national and international research and development projects in the design and implementation of Trustworthy Computing Platforms, Hardware-assisted Security, IoT Security and Privacy, Applied Cryptography, and Trustworthy AI. Prof. Sadeghi has been serving as General or Program Chair and Program Committee member of major Information Security and Privacy and Design and Automation venues, such as ACM CCS, IEEE Security & Privacy, NDSS, USENIX Security, DAC, DATE, and ICCAD. He was Editor-In-Chief of IEEE Security and Privacy Magazine. Ahmad served on several editorial boards, such as ACM Transactions on Information & System Security (TISSEC), as Guest editor of the IEEE TCAD, ACM Books, and ACM DIOT. He is on the editorial board of ACM TODAES and ACM DTRAP. In 2008 Prof. Sadeghi was awarded the renowned German prize "Karl Heinz Beckurts" for his research on Trusted and Trustworthy Computing technology and its transfer to industrial practice. The award honors excellent scientific achievements with a high impact on industrial innovations in Germany. In 2010 his group received the German IT Security Competition Award. In 2018 he received the ACM SIGSAC Outstanding Contributions Award for dedicated research, education, and management leadership in the security community and pioneering contributions in content protection, mobile security, and hardware-assisted security. SIGSAC is ACM's Special Interest Group on Security, Audit, and Control. In 2021 he was honored with the Intel Academic Leadership Award at USENIX Security for his influential research in information and computer security, particularly hardware-assisted security. In 2022 he received the prestigious European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant.

47610.title: VP R&D
47610.bio:
Tiago Henriques, is a seasoned executive with a vast background in the tech industry, particularly in the fields of cybersecurity, cyber insurance, and data science. Tiago has been instrumental in shaping several cybersecurity and data science projects throughout his career. Currently, he is the VP of Research at Coalition, Inc., where he is responsible for building innovative risk signals for risk selection in underwriting and risk aggregation modeling. He also oversees a team of researchers in the areas of cybersecurity, software engineering, and machine learning/AI.

Before his current role, he served in various leadership positions within Coalition, Inc., including Head of Research, Director of Engineering - Security and Data Collection, and GM - Customer Security. In each of these roles, he drove innovations in risk selection, mitigation, large scale data collection, and managed diverse teams to achieve strategic objectives.

Prior to his tenure at Coalition, Inc., Tiago was the founder and CEO of BinaryEdge, a cybersecurity firm he successfully ran for over five years before it was acquired by Coalition.

32870.title: Security Engineer
32870.bio: Marion Marschalek is a Security Engineer at AWS. Prior to that she worked at Intel and held different positions in the threat detection industry, as a malware reverse engineer and incident responder. Her most noteworthy contribution is her analysis work on the malware 'Babar' and other representatives of a collection of French nation state malware, which was cited by a number of international news outlets and also got her listed as one of Forbes' "30under30" talents in the Technology Europe division in 2016. Marschalek is a frequent speaker at major security conferences, including Black Hat, DEF CON, HITB, RSA, and SyScan, among others. Until recently she was teaching reverse engineering classes at University of Applied Sciences St. Poelten, from where she graduated in 2011 with a Master's Degree in Information Security. In 2015 she started a hacker bootcamp for women titled BlackHoodie, which over the years established itself as a global initiative to attract more diverse talent to the security industry.

42356.title: Researcher
42356.bio: Erik Rye is a researcher and PhD student at the University of Maryland, where he is a member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Center (MC2) and is advised by Dave Levin. He enjoys artisanally-crafted packets and trying to make the Internet a better place. Dogs are his favorite animal.

42416.title: P.h.D Student
42416.bio: Qi Wang (@Eki) is a PhD student in the Institute for Network Sciences and Cyberspace at the Tsinghua University. He works in the Network and Information Security Lab (NISL) and is advised by Prof. JianJun Chen. He focuses on WEB security and network protocol security. His work has been recognized by security conferences such as Oakland S&P and CCS. He is also an active participant in CTF games. He has won awards such as the champion of the D^3CTF 2023, and the runner-up of the XCTF-Final 2024. Website: https://ieki.xyz

45208.title: Associate Professor
45208.bio: Xiang Li is an Associate Professor from Nankai University. His research interests include network security, protocol security, IPv6 security, DNS security, Internet measurement, network and protocol fuzzing, network vulnerability discovery and attack, and underground economy with 17 research papers. As the first author, he has published many research papers at all top-tier security conferences, including Oakland S&P, USENIX Security, CCS, NDSS, and Black Hat (Asia, USA, and Europe). He has obtained over 200 CVE/CNVD vulnerability numbers, more than $11,600 rewards, 340+ GitHub stars, multiple CERT reports, 100+ news coverage, and RFC acknowledgment. He received multiple prizes, such as 1st prize of IPv6 Technology Application Innovation Competition, 2nd prize of GeekCon 2023 DAF Contest, National Scholarship, Wang Dazhong Scholarship, and Tsinghua Outstanding Scholarship.

48381.title: Ph.D. Candidate
48381.bio: Hello, I am Chuhan Wang, a 5th year Ph.D. student at the Network and Information Security Lab (NISL) of Tsinghua University, advised by Prof. Haixin Duan and Assistant Prof. Jianjun Chen. Now, I am a visiting scholar at University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, working with Prof. Gang Wang. My research interests include Web Security, Network Security, and Internet Measurement. Currently, I focus on email-related security research. I have published 6 papers at all top-tier academic conferences on network security, including Oakland S&P, USENIX Security, CCS, NDSS. My research results have helped Google, Apple, Yandex, Tencent, Shopee and other well-known Internet companies to fix vulnerabilities. As a member of Redbud, a CTF team belonging to Tsinghua University, I have won the ByteCTF 2020 championship and other CTF awards. Website: https://www.wangchuhan.cn

34757.title: Principal Research Scientist
34757.bio: Vasilios Mavroudis is a Principal Research Scientist and co-leads the AI for Cyberdefense (AICD) Research Center at the Alan Turing Institute. His team operates at the intersection of Cybersecurity and Machine Learning, working to enhance autonomous network defense. His research results have been published in top-tier academic and industrial venues. Beyond his core research focus, he has made significant contributions in diverse areas, including cryptographic hardware, ultrasonic tracking, blockchain technology and technical considerations of market fairness and manipulation. Vasilios holds a PhD in Computer Security from the Information Security Group at University College London. You can follow Vasilios on X (formerly Twitter) @mavroudisv

48261.title: Assistant Professor
48261.bio: Dr Jamie Gawith is an Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering at the University of Bath, UK, where he teaches power electronics, machine design, and advanced electronic materials. Prior to this, he was a Senior Integration Engineer at Tokamak Energy, developing nuclear fusion technology and a Visiting Researcher at Imperial College London, developing wireless charging systems. Dr Gawith obtained his PhD in Electrical Engineering from the University of Cambridge, where his research focused on superconducting wireless power supplies. He has authored or co-authored over 30 publications across the fields of nuclear fusion, applied superconductivity and wireless power, is named on several patents, and has given invited talks at international conferences in these fields.

48598.title: AI Security PhD Candidate
48598.bio: Sañyam Vyas is a highly motivated and dedicated AI Security PhD student with a passion for making the digital realm a safer and more resilient space. Sañyam is a PhD Student at Cardiff University (with Airbus Group) researching Automated Cyber Defence and Deep Reinforcement Learning Security and is a Visiting Machine Learning Researcher at The Alan Turing Institute, London, researching Deep Reinforcement Learning Security.

48599.title: Co-lead, AICD Research Centre
48599.bio: Chris Hicks is the co-lead of the AI for Cyber Defence (AICD) research centre at the Alan Turing Institute which aims to solve computer security and privacy problems using autonomous decision making. With an emphasis on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), our centre is focused on building autonomous cyber agents (AKA CAGE fighting) for security and privacy research. Long-term, Chris' ambition is to transform the science and practice of computer security through applied and fundamental advances in machine learning.

48133.title: PhD Student
48133.bio: Dalya Manatova studies organizational and social dynamics of cybercrime communities and computational methods for threat intel.

37968.title: Professor
37968.bio: Jean Camp is a Professor at the Luddy School of Computing, Informatics, and Engineering at Indiana University. Her research goal is the security that people need, the privacy they want, in systems they can trust. This requires risk identification, mitigation, and decision-making informed by risk communication. She is a Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers, a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science, a Fellow of the ACM, and has been inducted into Sigma Xi, The Scientific Research Honor Society. She joined Indiana after eight years at Harvard's Kennedy School where her courses were also listed in Harvard Law, Harvard Business, and the Engineering Systems Division of MIT. She spent the year after earning her doctorate from Carnegie Mellon as a Senior Member of the Technical Staff at Sandia National Laboratories. She began her career as an engineer at Catawba Nuclear Station and with a MSEE at University of North Carolina at Charlotte

45791.title: Staff Security Researcher
45791.bio: Nick Frichette is a Staff Security Researcher at Datadog, where he specializes in offensive AWS security. He is known for finding multiple zero-day vulnerabilities in AWS services and regularly publishing on new attack techniques. In addition to his research, Nick is the creator and primary contributor to Hacking the Cloud, an open source encyclopedia of offensive security capabilities for cloud environments. He is also a part of the AWS Community Builder Program, where he develops content on AWS security.

48121.title: Former NATO Analyst
48121.bio: Franky Saegerman has worked for NATO over 30 years in different capacities/functions most recently as IEA analyst, Head of Digital Insights and Head of Social Media.

33751.title: CEO
33751.bio: Jun Li is CEO at GoGoByte and a former Senior Security Research Expert at Qihoo 360, specializing in areas such as connected vehicles, wireless communications, and hardware. Jun is a core member of the 360 Unicorn Team and led the team in uncovering vulnerabilities in Tesla vehicles, earning induction into the Tesla Security Hall of Fame in 2018. Jun participated in the IoT Security Challenge by MITRE Corporation, achieving sixth place globally.

48113.title: Wireless Security Researcher
48113.bio: Zhongjie Wu is a wireless security researcher at GoGoByte. He mainly performs security tests on vehicle wireless interfaces, such as PEPS systems and RKE systems. He has also participated in the development of the security products of GoGoByte, mainly working on the RF and LF wireless test cases. He has mounted successful wireless relay tests in production vehicles from BMW and Tesla. He holds a bachelor's degree in Optoelectronic Engineering at the UESTC, China, and a master's diploma in Electric and Electronic Engineering at the University of Surrey, UK.

48105.title: Connected Vehicle Cybersecurity Researcher
48105.bio: Yuqiao Yang is a connected vehicle cybersecurity researcher at GoGoByte, a cybersecurity company dedicated to maintaining automobile security from silicon to cloud. He conducts penetration tests on automobile parts, does research on Internet of Vehicles cybersecurity and has obtained numerous patents. Security products of GoGoByte, which he participated in the development of, have been adopted by many OEMs and suppliers. He holds a bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering and is studying for a master's degree in Computer Science at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

48165.title: CTO
48165.bio: WenHao Liu is CTO at GoGoByte. WenHao graduated from the Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences and he is proficient in network traffic analysis, attack and defense. WenHao worked as a technical expert in Tencent, Qihoo 360, Alibaba and other well-known enterprises, with rich experience in full-stack development, security product architecture design and engineering.

48602.title: Security Engineer
48602.bio: Ruicong Shi is a security engineer at GoGoByte, specializing in penetration testing for in-vehicle networks and web/cloud platforms. He has conducted penetration testing on automotive components or complete vehicles for many major automotive OEMs and Tierx, and has successfully identified critical vulnerabilities.

45599.title: Technical Director
45599.company: CATARC Intelligent and Connected Technology Co., Ltd.
45599.bio: Yuqiao Ning is the Technical Director of CATARC Intelligent and Connected Technology Co., Ltd. He has extensive experience in computer systems and software security research. In his current role, he is primarily responsible for pioneering research in automotive penetration technology and the development of automated detection tools. His work focuses on analyzing security risks within automotive open-source software, with a particular emphasis on understanding the critical intersection of automotive security vulnerabilities and functional safety. He has played a pivotal role in organizing numerous automotive information security attack and defense challenges, contributing significantly to the advancement of safer and more secure automotive technologies. Furthermore, he has played an instrumental role in shaping national automotive information security standards, contributing to the drafting of several key national standards.

48603.title: Laboratory Director, Intelligent Testing Department
48603.company: China Merchants Testing Vehicle Technology Research Institute Co., Ltd.
48603.bio: Dr. Wu Chao is the Laboratory Director of the Intelligent Testing Department at China Merchants Testing Vehicle Technology Research Institute Co., Ltd. With a strong background in the field of connected vehicle security, he leads a team focused on the security and compliance aspects of connected automotive technologies. Dr. Wu brings a wealth of experience to his role, having been involved in the security testing and compliance processes for connected vehicles. His contributions extend to the development of national standards, where his insights have helped shape the industry's approach to security and regulation. His work is instrumental in guiding the research institute's efforts to enhance the security and reliability of intelligent connected vehicle systems.

48604.title: Security Researcher
48604.bio: Harry Guo is an experienced vehicle cybersecurity engineer with a solid foundation in cybersecurity and a profound understanding of the vehicle security domain. He graduated from the North University of China with a major in cybersecurity and possesses a professional technical background along with certifications such as ITIL. The vulnerabilities he has submitted have been recognized and included by CAVD and CNVD.

35653.title: ZJU100 Young Professor
35653.bio: Kun Yang received his Bachelor of Natural Science degree from the University of Science and Technology of China and his Doctor of Philosophy degree from the University of Florida. He served as a Sr. Security Architect at NVIDIA Corporation from May 2018 to January 2022. He joined Zhejiang University as a ZJU100 Young Professor in March 2022. His research interests include intelligent connected vehicle security, SoC/CPU/GPU security architecture, and secure converged architecture of software and hardware. The symmetric crypto accelerator that he was in charge of developing and the asymmetric crypto accelerator that he participated in developing have been integrated into the latest NVIDIA Drive AGX Orin and NVIDIA Grace CPU. He is chairing multiple national-level and enterprise-funded research projects. He is a recipient of the 2022 Hangzhou West Lake Pearl Project Overseas High-Level Young Talent, 2022 Zhejiang University Qizhen Outstanding Young Scholar, 2021 NVIDIA Patent Award, 2020 NVIDIA NTECH Conference Best Paper Award (1st Place), and 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Hardware Oriented Security and Trust (HOST) Best Paper Award Nomination.

48605.title: Professor
48605.bio: Prof. Xiaohang Wang's research area includes optimization for chiplet-based many-core systems and automotive security. He was the co-organizer of NoCArc conference, and the special session chair of NoCS 2018/2022 and APCCAS 2018. He was the recipient of PDP 2015 and VLSI-SoC 2014 best paper awards. He focused on simulator modeling for million-core-level multi-chiplet systems, inter- and intra-chiplet topology and routing algorithm design, and designed an intrusion detection system for automotive buses.

48625.title: Qiushi Chair Professor
48625.bio: Kui Ren, Qiushi Chair Professor of Zhejiang University, AAAS, ACM, CCF, and IEEE Fellow, is currently the dean of the College of Computer Science and Technology of Zhejiang University and the executive deputy director of the State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security. Professor Kui Ren is mainly engaged in research in data security and privacy protection, AI security, and security in intelligent devices and vehicular networks. He has presided over major domestic and foreign scientific research projects such as the Ministry of Science and Technology, the National Natural Science Foundation of China, and the National Science Foundation of the United States. He has won the First Prize of Zhejiang Provincial Natural Science Award, the First Prize in Natural Science of the Chinese Institute of Electronics Science and Technology Award, the first Guohua Outstanding Scholar Award of Zhejiang University, and the CISTC Technology Achievement Award of the IEEE Communications Society. He has published over 400 peer-reviewed journal and conference articles, with an H-Index of 94 and more than 49,000 citations.

40804.title: Chang jiang Scholars
40804.company: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
40804.bio: Professor Chen Ting is a distinguished professor and doctoral supervisor at the University of Electronic Science and Technology, a recipient of the Ministry of Education Young Changjiang Scholars Award, Sichuan Province Outstanding Youth, and Chengdu Rongcheng Talent. He has been honored with the 2022 Alibaba DAMO Academy Orange Award, the 2022 CCF Young Scientist Award, the 2012 National Science and Technology Progress Second Prize, and the 2010 Sichuan Province Science and Technology Progress First Prize. He is engaged in research on software security, particularly focusing on the security of blockchain software, Android software, and desktop system software. In the past five years, he has published more than 40 papers in CCF A international conferences and journals, and has received 15 academic/competition awards, including the Best Paper Award at INFOCOM 2018. He has presided over one National Natural Science Fund key project, two key research and development projects of the Ministry of Science and Technology, and multiple provincial and ministerial projects, as well as 9 horizontal projects, including three horizontal projects in cooperation with Ant Zhixin (Hangzhou) Information Technology Co., Ltd.

48368.title: Research Assistant
48368.company: The University of Texas at Dallas
48368.bio: Josh Wiedemeier is a second-year Computer Science Ph.D. student at the University of Texas at Dallas, advised by Dr. Kangkook Jee. Josh's research primarily focuses on reverse engineering Python bytecode, with a secondary focus in system provenance analysis.

48765.title: Student at The University of Texas at Dallas

48769.company: The University of Texas at Dallas

41162.company: The University of Texas at Dallas

48415.title: Research Assistant
48415.bio: Kai Tu is a PhD student at Pennsylvania State University. He is experienced in analyzing cellular network protocols. His research includes analyzing 4G/5G commercial baseband chipsets for security issues.

48483.title: Research Assistant
48483.bio: Yilu Dong is a security researcher currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in the SyNSec lab at Penn State University. He has focused on the security of 5G systems and worked on multiple projects to improve the security and privacy of both UE and Core Network implementations.

48485.title: Research Assistant
48485.bio: Abdullah Al Ishtiaq is a third-year Ph.D. student at Pennsylvania State University. His primary research interest is in the security of wireless networks and natural language processing. His recent work involves analyzing protocol specifications for security issues and detecting vulnerabilities and noncompliance in 4G/5G and BLE devices.

48486.title: Research Assistant
48486.bio: Syed Md Mukit Rashid is a second-year Ph.D. student in Computer Science at Penn State, specializing in computer security with a keen focus on advancing testing frameworks. His primary research focuses on enhancing the security of protocol implementations such as 4G LTE, 5G cellular networks, and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) stacks. He also has a Master's degree in the same field. He aims to identify and repair critical security vulnerabilities within protocol implementations, leveraging program analysis techniques and the power of LLMs.

48487.title: Graduate Researcher
48487.bio: Weixuan Wang is a master's student in computer science at Pennsylvania State University and is currently a member of SyNSec Lab. His research interests include network and software security.

48488.title: Research Assistant
48488.bio: Tianwei Wu, a Ph.D. student at Penn State, concentrates on the security aspects of emerging wireless technologies such as LTE, 5G, and BLE. His work primarily involves exploring potential attacks, developing robust defense mechanisms, and identifying incorrect implementations by vendors.

39747.title: Assistant Professor
39747.bio: Syed Rafiul Hussain is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Pennsylvania State University. His research interests broadly lie in network and systems security. Prior to joining Penn State, he completed his Ph.D. at Purdue University in the fall of 2018 and has since been recognized with the NSF CAREER Award and the DARPA Young Faculty Award in 2022. His research impacts the design of 4G and 5G standards and is featured by the FCC and over 100 media outlets.

48913.title: Cyber Product Lead
48913.bio: Bridget Quinn Choi is the Lead Product Counsel for the Cyber Technology and Media team at Woodruff Sawyer an insurance broker, where she works with Woodruff Sawyer clients to find and customize insurance solutions to fit their unique business needs. In her career, Ms. Choi has lead US Cyber underwriting team, she has also served as the Director of Strategy for the Resilience and Incident Response team at Booz Allen Hamilton. She has served as general counsel for Kivu Consulting, a money service business, cyber incident response, and consulting firm. Ms. Choi began her career as a litigator in New York City and has served as a claim counsel and claims leader for two major insurance carriers. Ms. Choi is admitted to the New York State Bar as well as the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York.

48613.title: Senior Security Researcher
48613.bio: Maxime Villard is a security researcher who works at the Microsoft Offensive Research & Security Engineering (MORSE) team. He specializes in low-level platform security and has a proven track record of finding, developing ways to find, and exploiting, critical vulnerabilities in complex systems.

36978.title: Principal Security Research Manager
36978.bio: Yair Netzer is a principal security research manager at Microsoft, working as part of the Edge & Platform Security Fundamentals organization. Yair manages 2 security research teams, focusing on both cloud and OS security. As part of this role, Yair led multiple engagements with Microsoft's partners, ensuring the root of trust for client and server devices is as secure as intended. Before Microsoft, Yair spent 14 years at Intel, as a security researcher, and later as a security manager - within the CSME firmware team, reviewing the root of trust for all Intel shipped products.

47654.title: Senior Security Researcher
47654.bio: Ben Hania is a senior security researcher at Microsoft, working as part of the Edge & Platform Security Fundamentals organization. Ben's research focuses on finding vulnerabilities and design flaws in firmware and architecture of embedded devices. Ben has accumulated over a decade of experience in security research, both prior to and during his time at Microsoft.

34467.title: Principal Threat Researcher
34467.bio: Daniel Bohannon is a Principal Threat Researcher on Permiso Security's P0 Labs team with over fourteen years of information security experience, including incident response consulting at MANDIANT, security research at FireEye and threat hunting at Microsoft. After a decade of focusing on endpoint security, he now leads a team of Albania- and Kosovo-based cloud threat researchers focused on obfuscation, evasion and detection capabilities in various combinations of PaaS, IaaS, SaaS and IdP solutions. He is the author of the Invoke-Obfuscation, Invoke-CradleCrafter and Invoke-DOSfuscation open-source obfuscation frameworks and co-author of the Revoke-Obfuscation PowerShell obfuscation detection framework and the Cloud Console Cartographer defensive visibility framework. He has presented at numerous conferences around the world including Black Hat USA, Black Hat Asia & DEF CON. Mr. Bohannon received a Master of Science in Information Security from the Georgia Institute of Technology (2013) and a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from The University of Georgia (2010).

47778.title: Senior Cyber Security Engineer
47778.bio: Sabajete Elezaj is a Senior Cyber Security Engineer at Solaris SE with a background in cybersecurity extending over 6 years. Her expertise spans incident response, threat hunting and blue team operations. Her work focuses on enhancing cyber defense strategies. Mrs. Elezaj holds a Master of Science in Information Security from the University of Tirana. She has also shared her expertise at cybersecurity conferences, including BSides Tirana.

42634.title: Security Researcher
42634.bio: Maxime Rossi Bellom (@max_r_b) is a Security Researcher and Tech Lead working at Quarkslab, focusing on the hardware and low level software security of mobile devices and embedded systems. He loves playing with secure boot, and security chips embedded in smartphones.

48573.title: Security Researcher
48573.bio: Raphael Neveu is a security researcher working at Quarkslab and focusing on low-level mobile software.

42674.title: Security Researcher
42674.bio: Damiano Melotti (@DamianoMelotti) is a security researcher. He is mostly interested in systems security, especially in mobile platforms (Android) and automated vulnerability research.

38103.title: Security Engineer
38103.bio: Gabrielle Viala (@pwissenlit) is a security engineer specializing in vulnerability research and exploitation at Quarkslab. She is usually focused on desktop-based components, but as long as the project involves low-level technology, any target can be a good playground for her.

47784.title: Partner
47784.bio: Jess Nall is one of the country's foremost experts with regard to federal criminal and regulatory liability for information security professionals, especially Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs). Jess has personally represented more CISOs and InfoSec leaders and team members in high-profile federal investigations and follow on civil actions than any other lawyer in the U.S. Jess presently serves as a senior partner in Baker McKenzie's government enforcement defense practice, with a focus and deep expertise in defending against personal and enterprise liability in the areas of cyber security and AI.

46684.title: Senior Threat Researcher
46684.bio: Maël Le Touz is a Senior Threat Researcher at Infoblox where he specializes in the detection of threats as they manifest in the domain name system (DNS). His background is in financial fraud investigation and he has strong experience in reverse engineering. He previously reverse engineered critical components of the Decoy Dog malware that confirmed the DNS C2 was distinct from the open source Pupy project.

45968.title: Vice President Threat Intelligence
45968.bio: Dr. Burton is the head of Infoblox Threat Intel and specializes in research of cybercriminal activity through passive DNS (pDNS) analysis. She joined Infoblox in 2018 after spending 22 years with the National Security Agency (NSA) where she used her background in mathematics to address a wide range of problems in intelligence.

48061.title: Offensive Security Senior Manager
48061.bio: Hao Wang has more than 12 years of cyber threat management experience including attack and penetration testing, vulnerability management, threat hunting, incident response, and bug bounty program management. He is currently leading the threat emulation team in PayPal and is responsible for conducting attack and penetration testing including cloud security, red team, purple team, internal / external on-prem infrastructure, and application / API assessments for all of PayPal's business units. In addition, his team supports the Bug Bounty program run by both PayPal and HackerOne. Hao has presented at the following conferences: SANS Threat Hunting 2016 - APT Hunter: Enabling the hunt for abnormalities, ISACA Spring Conference 2017 - Using Incident Response Tactics to Enhance Enterprise Breach Awareness, Troopers 2018 - Attack and Defend Microsoft Enhanced Security Administrative Environment, BSidesLV 2018 - Overlooked Tactics for Attacking Hardened Active Directory Environment and NA CACS 2019 - Identifying Critical Flaws in Hardened Active Directory Environment.

48062.title: Offensive Security Engineer
48062.bio: Caleb Sargent is a seasoned cybersecurity professional, boasting over 8 years of experience in threat emulation. He specializes in various areas, including red teaming, purple teaming, penetration testing, and physical security assessments. Previously a consultant at Optiv where he obtained the OSCP, and currently serving as an Offensive Security Engineer at PayPal, Caleb orchestrates and executes red team engagements by focusing on enhancing security effectiveness through purple team engagements within both cloud and internal networks. Caleb demonstrates his ability to identify vulnerabilities and mitigate risks through active participation in bug bounty programs on platforms like HackerOne and PayPal, contributing as both a researcher and in supportive roles. Additionally, he has refined his skills through endpoint detection and response testing, further enhancing his expertise in cybersecurity. Caleb has presented the following talks: Optiv Team Summit 2018 - OSINT from the Ground Up, Optiv Team Summit 2019 - Bypassing Windows Defender, Optiv Team Summit 2020 - Data Security for Consulting and PayPal ECS Conference 2021 - Anatomy of a Red Team Engagement.

48634.title: Lead Threat Detection Engineer
48634.bio: Harrison Pomeroy has 10 years of cybersecurity experience ranging from Fraud Investigation Analyst, Cybersecurity Analyst, Incident Response Engineer, Threat Hunting, and Threat Detection. He is currently the Lead Engineer for the Threat Detection Team, which is responsible for developing and managing detection, incident response capabilities, automated prevention capabilities, cloud-based threat detection, automated intelligence frameworks, detection research and operationalizing security tools. In addition to these responsibilities, his team directly supports the Cybersecurity Defense Center, Cyber Threat Management, Threat Hunting, Threat Intelligence, and Offensive Security's Purple Team. Harrison demonstrates his abilities through developing custom detection frameworks, and intelligence that enables the platform to automate the prevention of large-scale abuse. Additionally, he consistently refines detection strategy and maturity to uplift the discipline within the organization to ensure PayPal can identify emerging and novel threats.

48059.title: Senior Director, Global Cyber Operations
48059.bio: Renana Friedlich is the Senior Director of Cyber Threat Management at PayPal, leading a global team of security experts . Renana has over 19 years of public and private sector cybersecurity experience, earning a reputation for delivering innovative cybersecurity solutions. She served in elite intelligence unit with the Israeli Defense forces, where she gained invaluable experience and contributed to national security efforts. Her extensive experience in breach investigations, privacy, and M&A has been pivotal in safeguarding Fortune 500 clients as part of her consulting role with Ernst and Young. She actively engages in shaping the future of cybersecurity through speaking at Security conferences and her advisory board roles at leading universities, tech companies, and startups.

44552.title: Security Researcher
44552.bio: Nan Wang (@eternalsakura13) is a senior security researcher at the 360 Vulnerability Research Institute. His main focus is on hunting for vulnerabilities in the Chrome browser and finding ways to exploit them. He consistently ranked as a Chrome Top10 VRP Researcher for 2021, 2022, and 2023, and was also recognized by Facebook as a Top3 whitehat hacker in 2023. He has also been a speaker at security conferences, including Black Hat Asia 2023 and Black Hat USA 2023.

45176.title: Master Candidate
45176.bio: Zhenghang Xiao (@Kipreyyy) is a 1st-year Master's candidate at the Institute of Network Science and Cyberspace, Tsinghua University, belonging to the Network and Information Security Lab (NISL). He has a keen interest in browser security and fuzzing, and he successfully discovered several vulnerabilities and assigned CVE IDs, being acknowledged by major companies such as Google, Facebook, and other notable vendors. Also, he ranked as a Google Chrome VRP Top4 researcher in 2023 and got his presentations accepted by top industry security conferences like Black Hat USA 2023.

47903.title: Security Research Intern
47903.bio: Xuehao Guo (@gxh191) is a Security Researcher and former CTF Player @Syclover.

48497.title: PhD Student
48497.bio: Qinrun Dai is pursuing a Ph.D. with Prof. Yueqi Chen in the Computer Science Department at the University of Colorado, Boulder. Qinrun's current research is formalizing exploitation to enhance Linux Kernel security, and finding and exploiting logical bugs on Windows system. Additionally, Qinrun has gained rich experience in evaluating the security mechanisms of micro-kernel-based systems like Windows Kernel, Zircon, and Harmony OS. Qinrun was a CTF player and leader @ team L3H_Sec, focusing on Reverse Engineering and Pwn.

48278.title: Founder & CEO
48278.bio: HD Moore is a pioneer of the cybersecurity industry who has dedicated his career to vulnerability research, network discovery, and software development since the 1990s. He is most recognized for creating Metasploit and is a passionate advocate for open-source software and vulnerability disclosure. HD serves as the CEO and co-founder of runZero, a provider of cutting-edge cyber asset attack surface management (CAASM) software and cloud services. Prior to founding runZero, he held leadership positions at Atredis Partners, Rapid7, and BreakingPoint. HD's professional journey began with exploring telephone networks, developing exploits for the Department of Defense, and breaking into financial institutions. When he's not working, he enjoys hacking on weird Go projects, building janky electronics, running in circles, and playing single-player RPGs.

32515.title: Director of Security Research
32515.bio: Rob King is the Director of Security Research at runZero. Over his career, Rob has served as a senior researcher with KoreLogic, the architect for TippingPoint DVLabs, and helped get several startups off the ground. Rob helped design SC Magazine's Data Leakage Prevention Product of the Year for 2010, and was awarded the 3Com Innovator of the Year Award in 2009. He has been invited to speak at Black Hat, Shmoocon, SANS Network Security, and USENIX.

47278.title: Senior Red Team TL
47278.bio: Dr. Amanda Minnich is a Senior Red Team TL at Microsoft on the Microsoft AI Red Team, where she red teams Microsoft's foundational models and Copilots for safety and security vulnerabilities. Prior to Microsoft, Dr. Minnich worked at Twitter, focusing on identifying international election interference and other types of abuse and spam campaigns using graph clustering algorithms. She also previously worked at Sandia National Laboratories and Mandiant, where she applied machine learning research techniques to malware classification and malware family identification. Dr. Minnich is heavily involved with tech outreach efforts, especially for women in tech. She received her MS and PhD in Computer Science with Distinction from the University of New Mexico.

49120.title: Senior Director, AI and Legal Ethics
49120.bio: Nikki Pope is in-house counsel at NVIDIA and leads the company's Trustworthy AI initiative. Prior to joining NVIDIA, Nikki was the managing director of the High-Tech Law Institute at Santa Clara University and an attorney at Cooley LLP for 10 years, and on the faculty at Santa Clara Law. Nikki has also held management positions in large companies and startups in financial services, entertainment, consumer products, and web-based services and applications.

48404.title: Research Scientist
48404.bio:
Mikel Rodriguez has spent over two decades working in the public and private sector securing the application of Artificial Intelligence in high-stakes consequential environments. At Google DeepMind, Mikel defines and leads the cross-functional AI Security Red and Blue "ReBl" team to ensure that foundational models are battle-tested with the rigor and scrutiny of real-world adversaries, and help drive research and tooling that will make this red-blue mindset scalable in preparation for AGI.

In his role as the Managing Director at MITRE Labs, Mikel built and led the AI Red Team for the Department of Defense that focused on deployed AI systems that can be susceptible to attacks involving evasion, data poisoning, model replication; and the exploitation of software flaws to deceive, manipulate, compromise, and render them ineffective. Mikel's team worked on developing methods to mitigate bias and defend against emerging ML attacks, securing the AI supply chain, and generally ensuring the trustworthiness of AI systems so they perform as intended in mission-critical environments. While at MITRE, his team in collaboration with many industry partners, published ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems) - a knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and case studies for machine learning (ML) systems based on real-world observations, demonstrations from ML red teams and security groups, and the state of the possible from academic research. Mikel firmly believes that AI's potential will only be realized through collaborations that help produce reliable, resilient, fair, interpretable, privacy preserving, and secure technologies.

Mikel received his Ph.D. in 2010 while working at University of Central Florida's computer vision lab with professor Mubarak Shah. He then moved to Paris where he worked as a post-doctoral research fellow at INRIA.

46384.title: Head of Claims and Incident Response for Cyber
46384.bio: Catherine Lyle is the Head of Claims and Incident Response for Cyber within Tokio Marine HCC- Cyber & Professional Lines Group. With more than 25 years of claims experience, Lyle’s work focuses on leading a team that ensures the quick resolution of cyber events and claims, as well litigation involving professional liability policies for technology, media, and telecommunication companies. She is a frequent speaker and published author regarding cyber law and claims. Prior to joining Tokio Marine HCC- CPLG, Lyle was the Head of Claims at Coalition and was an attorney for General Electric as well as an Assistant Attorney General for The Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Lyle is a member of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and Colorado Bars.

31839.title: Global Head of Security Research
31839.bio: Daniel Cuthbert loves doing security research. With a career spanning over 20 years on both the offensive and defensive side, he's seen the evolution of hacking from a small groups of curious minds to organized criminal networks and nation state we see today. He is the original co-author of the OWASP Testing Guide, released in 2003 and now the co-author of the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS) and sits on the UK Government Cybersecurity Advisory Board.

45164.title: Senior Security Researcher
45164.bio: Bohan Liu (@P4nda20371774) is a senior security researcher at Tencent Security Xuanwu Lab. He focuses on browser security research, discovered multiple Chrome vulnerabilities, and was in the top 20 of Chrome VRP Researchers in 2023 and he is the winner of the Mobile Phone category in Tianfu Cup 2023. He has also presented his research results at security conferences such as DEFCON 31, Black Hat Europe 2023, and Black Hat Asia 2024.

45134.title: Security Researcher
45134.bio: Zheng Wang (@xmzyshypnc) is a senior Security Researcher at Tencent Security Xuanwu Lab. He's mainly engaged in browser and Linux kernel security. He was also a speaker at Black Hat Asia/Europe 2023.

45163.title: PhD Student
45163.bio: Yeqi Fu is a Ph.D student in the School of Computing at the National University of Singapore. Yeqi works on on PWN, Fuzz, and LLVM.

48306.title: Postdoctoral Researcher
48306.bio: Dr. Cen Zhang is a Research Fellow at Nanyang Technological University, specializing in software security. His research focuses on vulnerability detection techniques like fuzz testing. He earned his Ph.D. from the same university in August 2023. His work has been published in top-tier conferences of software security and software engineering, such as S&P, Usenix Security, CCS, ICSE, ASE, FSE, ISSTA, and WWW. Dr. Zhang's work has received several prestigious awards, including the ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper Awards of ASE 2023 and ICSE 2024.

34048.title: InfoSec Professor
34048.bio: Daniel Gruss (@lavados) is a Professor at Graz University of Technology. He has been teaching undergraduate courses since 2010. Daniel's research focuses on side channels and transient execution attacks. He implemented the first remote fault attack running in a website, known as Rowhammer.js. His research team was one of the teams that found the Meltdown and Spectre bugs published in early 2018. In 2023, he received an ERC Starting Grant to research the sustainability of security. He frequently speaks at top international venues.

47716.title: InfoSec Researcher
47716.bio: Stefan Gast is a PhD student at Graz University of Technology since 2021. His focus is on cybersecurity, especially in the areas of microarchitectural and remote side-channel attacks and how to defend against them. Stefan's work has been published at top international venues like IEEE Security and Privacy. Alongside his research, Stefan has been teaching for over ten years, showing his dedication to both learning and teaching in the field of cybersecurity.

47563.title: Offensive Security Team Lead
47563.bio: Jacob Larsen is an offensive security team lead at a distinguished Australian cyber security consulting firm, and prior to this was a lead in cyber governance, risk and compliance. He is also a threat researcher who has specialized in infiltrating underground cybercrime groups to gain insights into their tradecraft and motives since 2016. He has analyzed the modus operandi of doxxers, sim swappers, crypto drainers, fraud groups, espionage specialists, exploit developers, initial access brokers and more. Jacob is also a seasoned speaker, who has shared his research at conferences such as BSides Perth 2021, AISA Cyber Conference Melbourne 2022, and AISA Cyber Conference Canberra 2023.

46517.title: Senior Cloud Security Architect
46517.bio: Eric Woodruff, throughout his 24-year career in the IT field, has sought out and held a diverse range of roles, including technical manager in the public sector, Sr. Premier Field Engineer at Microsoft, and Security and Identity Architect in the Microsoft Partner ecosystem. Currently, he is a Sr. Cloud Security Architect working as part of the Security Research team at Semperis. Eric is a Microsoft MVP for security, recognized for his expertise in the Microsoft identity ecosystem. Outside of work, Eric supports the professional community, providing his insights and expertise at conferences, participating on the IDPro Body of Knowledge committee, and blogging about Entra and related cloud security topics.

44204.title: Threat Intelligence Analyst
44204.bio: Morgan Demboski is a Threat Intelligence Analyst for the Sophos Managed Detection and Response (MDR) team, where her focuses include tactical cyber intelligence, data enrichment, activity clustering, and monitoring emerging threats. With a Masters in Intelligence and Security Studies, her areas of interest span beyond the cyber realm to include geopolitics and international security. In past roles, Morgan worked in the Network Detection and Response (NDR) space, where she focused on tracking attack patterns, analyzing command-and-control infrastructure, and threat research reporting.

47878.title: Senior Threat Hunter
47878.bio: Mark Parsons is a Threat Hunter with Sophos' Managed Detection and Response service. He is regularly pursuing threat actors with a wide range of motivations across as many telemetry streams as he can find and enjoys collaborating with the Threat Intelligence, Detection Engineering, and Incident Response teams within MDR to track, and prevent novel and sophisticated threat actors. Outside of work, Mark is an avid snowboarder and loving dog dad.

38796.title: Security Engineer
38796.bio: Xiling Gong is a Security Researcher at Google on the Android Red Team. Xiling focuses on finding and exploiting vulnerabilities in the low-level components of the Android platform and Pixel devices. Xiling has been a speaker at CanSecWest 2018, Black Hat USA 2019, Def Con 27, Black Hat Asia 2021, Black Hat USA 2023, and Def Con 31.

43607.title: Manager of Android RedTeam
43607.bio: Xuan Xing is manager of Android RedTeam at Google. For the past several years, Xuan focused on finding security vulnerabilities in various low level components of Android/Pixel devices. He is passionate about software fuzzing for security research. In Black Hat USA 2022 Xuan presented "Google Reimagined a Phone. It was Our Job to Red Team and Secure it" talking about Pixel ABL security auditing.

32754.title: Technical Leader of Android RedTeam
32754.bio: Eugene Rodionov, PhD, is a Security Researcher at Google on the Android Red Team. In his current position, Eugene focuses on finding and exploiting vulnerabilities in the low-level components of the Android platform and Pixel devices. Prior to that, Rodionov performed offensive security research on UEFI firmware for Client Platforms at Intel, and ran internal research projects and performed in-depth analysis of complex threats at ESET. His fields of interest include reverse engineering, vulnerability analysis, firmware security and anti-rootkit technologies. Rodionov is a co-author of the "Rootkits and Bootkits: Reversing Modern Malware and Next Generation Threats" book and has spoken at security conferences such as Black Hat, DefCon, REcon, ZeroNights, and CARO.

46085.title: Security Researcher
46085.bio: Hillai Ben-Sasson is a security researcher based in Israel. As part of the Wiz Research Team, Hillai specializes in research and exploitation of web applications, application security, and finding vulnerabilities in complex high-level systems. You can reach him on X, formerly known as Twitter @hillai

42007.title: Security Researcher
42007.bio: Sagi Tzadik is a security researcher on the Wiz Research team. His expertise lies in identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities in web applications, as well as in network security and protocols. He has been recognized for his work and was featured on the MSRC Top Security Researcher Leaderboard. You can reach Safi on X, formerly known as Twitter, @sagitz_

45998.title: B.Sc. Student
45998.bio: Nadav Adir is a Technion - Institute of Technology BSc graduate with experience in security research. Nadav worked as a Cyber Security Engineer in Huawei's Endpoint Security team as well as an Internet Networking course staffer at the Technion. Nadav has competed on behalf of the Technion in the finals of the INCS-CoE's Country-to-Country Capture The Flag (CTF) Cyber Competition held at Keio University, Japan. Furthermore, Nadav was a professional Junior League Handball player.

41326.title: Security Researcher
41326.bio: Alon Dankner is a security researcher. At the age of 19, Alon graduated with a B.Sc. degree in computer science at the University of Haifa (cum laude) as part of "Etgar" program (Etgar means Challenge) for outstanding high school students. Subsequently, he completed an M.Sc. degree in computer science at the Technion (cum laude). Currently, Alon is a security researcher at Nokod Security, a low-code/no-code security startup. Computers and network security have always been a topic of interest to him, and his research focuses on network security and on the security of industrial control systems (ICS). This is Alon's fourth Black Hat, presenting advanced and new research in the field of ICS security.

39811.title: Professor
39811.bio: Prof. Eli Biham received his BSc in Mathematics and Computer Science at the Tel Aviv University (cum laude), 1982, and his PhD from the Weizmann Institute (1991). His PhD thesis developed Differential Cryptanalysis, the first cryptanalysis method that could break the Data Encryption Standard (DES), and the first general cryptanalysis method that was applicable to a large family of block ciphers. Since 1991 he has been a faculty member at the Technion's faculty of Computer Science. He (together with his students and colleagues) developed various methods for analysis of various kinds of ciphers. The most known of them are DES, and the cipher of the GSM cellular phone system (A5) - which proved that it is easy to listen in to any GSM (voice or data) conversation, and even to fake such calls as if originated from somebody else's phone. He also developed new ciphers, the most known of them is Serpent, which was a leading candidate to become the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) - the successor of DES. Eli Biham is the founding head of the Technion Hiroshi Fujiwara cyber security research center. He served in dozens of program committees, as the program and general chair of the FSE 1997 workshop, and as program chair of EUROCRYPT 2003 and SAC 2006. He was also an editor of the Journal of Cryptology and a director of the International Association for Cryptologic Research (IACR). Between 2008 and 2013 he served as the dean of the faculty of computer science. Since 2012 he has been an IACR fellow. He received the RSA award (2012) and holds the position of IACR distinguished lecturer (2013).
