39808.title: Senior Researcher
39808.bio: Dr. Sara Bitan is a senior researcher at the Technion Hiroshi Fujiwara Cyber Security Research Center. Her research interests include security of embedded systems, including PLCs, vehicle ECUs, and trusted execution environments. Sara has over 20 years of experience in the cyber-security industry. She was the V.P. of Research and Development of a network security startup and worked as a security architect at Microsoft. Sara is a co-founder of CyCloak, which provides advanced cyber-security solutions. Sara has a BA, MSc, and PhD from the computer science faculty in the Technion in Haifa Israel.

48550.title: Security Researcher
48550.bio: Ron Freudenthal is a vulnerability researcher with over a decade of hands-on experience. Originating from the field of Signal Processing and EW, he successfully exploited communication hardware, navigation systems, ICS/SCADA infrastructure, mobile devices and automotive ICUs. When not picking apart complex systems, Ron enjoys biking, skiing and recovering from various related accidents.

46000.title: M.Sc. Student
46000.bio: Or Keret is an MSc student at the Technion with experience in security research.

48914.title: Partner and Vice Chair of Cybersecurity and Data Privacy

47153.title: Managing Director
47153.bio:
Scott Stransky is Managing Director and Head of the Marsh McLennan Cyber Risk Intelligence Center.

The Center launched in 2021 to provide cyber modeling, thought leadership, and cyber analytics guidance across Marsh McLennan. Under his leadership, the Center leverages Marsh McLennan’s proprietary data sets and external data sources, and combines them with advanced machine learning algorithms, stochastic modeling techniques, and Monte Carlo simulations, to develop a robust suite of models for managing cyber risk.

Previously, he led the Cyber Modeling group at extreme event modeling firm AIR Worldwide (part of Verisk Analytics).

He is a recognized speaker across North America and Europe on the topics of cyber insurance risk and catastrophe modeling, having been invited to speak at numerous conferences sponsored by Advisen, NetDiligence, IUA of London, RAA, CPCU Society, AM Best, Lloyd's, Black Hat, and others, in addition to engaging directly with clients.

He was voted by his industry peers to be the 2023 Cyber Risk Industry Person of the Year in the Actuary/Modeler category. Mr. Stransky earned a bachelor’s degree in Mathematics with Computer Science from MIT and a master’s degree in Atmospheric Science from MIT.

48949.title: Founder
48949.bio: Moxie Marlinspike is the founder of Signal.

32054.title: Founder of Black Hat and U.S. Department of Homeland Security Advisory Council
32054.company: U.S. Department of Homeland Security Advisory Council
32054.bio: Jeff Moss advises companies on security issues, both, electronic and physical, as well as speaking globally on the topic. He sits on several advisory boards helping enterprises make informed decisions on cyber risks. In April 2011 Mr. Moss was appointed as the Chief Security Officer for the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), a non-profit whose responsibilities include coordinating and ensuring the security, stability and resiliency of the Internet's unique global identifiers as well as maintaining the root zone of the Internet. This position involved managing the IT security of the ICANN networks and information systems, the physical security of ICANN facilities and meetings, and ensuring that ICANN meets its security and resiliency commitments to the multi stake holder community that oversees ICANN. This position involved extensive international travel and coordination with governments, law enforcement, and operational security communities in support of discussions around Internet Governance and security. Mr. Moss left this position at the end of 2013. Moss is the founder and creator of both Black Hat and DEF CON, two of the most influential information security conferences in the world, attracting over ten thousand people from around the world to learn the latest in security technology from those researchers who create it. Prior to creating Black Hat, Jeff was a director at Secure Computing Corporation where he helped establish their Professional Services Department in the United States, Asia, and Australia. His primary work was security assessments of large multi-national corporations. Jeff has also worked for Ernst & Young, LLP in their Information System Security division. Because of this unique background Jeff is uniquely qualified with his ability to bridge the gap between the underground researcher community and law enforcement, between the worlds of pure research and the responsible application of disclosure. Jeff is currently a member of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Advisory Council (HSAC), providing advice and recommendations to the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security on matters related to homeland security. Jeff is a life member of the Council on Foreign Relations, which is an independent, nonpartisan membership organization, think tank, and publisher. In 2013, Jeff was appointed as a Nonresident Senior Fellow at the Atlantic Council, associated with the Cyber Statecraft Initiative, within the Brent Scowcroft Center on International Security. In 2014, Jeff joined the Georgetown University School of Law School Cybersecurity Advisory Committee. Jeff is also active in the World Economic Forum, and recently became a member of the Cyber Security Global Agenda Council for 2014-2016. In addition, Jeff earned the ICSA President's Award for Public Service in 2011.

46991.title: Senior Security Researcher
46991.bio: Vladimir Tokarev is a seasoned senior security researcher, specializing in IoT/OT, Windows, and Linux vulnerabilities research. With extensive experience in cybersecurity, Vladimir has demonstrated a keen ability to identify and address critical security issues in various systems. In early 2023, Vladimir presented his research titled "CoDe16: 16 Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Affecting CODESYS Framework, Leading to Remote Code Execution on Millions of Industrial Devices Across Industries". This comprehensive study focused on vulnerabilities within the widely used CODESYS framework, revealing potential risks to industrial devices across different sectors. Vladimir's meticulous analysis uncovered a total of 31 new vulnerabilities, highlighting the importance of proactive security measures in OT environments. In addition to his research on CODESYS, Vladimir has contributed to enhancing security in other critical systems. He discovered two new vulnerabilities in the Windows Driver of Foxboro DCS Control Core Services and one new vulnerability in SFPMONITOR.SYS, a component used by SonicWall products. Furthermore, Vladimir has identified vulnerabilities in TP-Link products, further extending his expertise in securing diverse systems. Twitter: @G1ND1L4

37467.title: CISO
37467.bio: Lester Godsey is the Chief Information Security and Privacy Officer for Maricopa County, AZ, the fourth most populous and fastest growing county in the United States. With over twenty-eight years of higher education and local government IT experience, it is safe to say that responding to the cybersecurity and physical threats from the 2020 elections has been the most challenging but fulfilling experience of his professional career. When not responding to mis, dis and mal information campaigns he can be found speaking at local, state, and national conferences on topics ranging from telecommunications to project management to cybersecurity and data. Lester has taught at the collegiate level for over twelve years in the areas of technology, business, project management, and cybersecurity. The author of numerous trade journals and online magazine articles, he is CISM and PMP certified as well as holding a BA in Music and a MS in Technology, both from Arizona State University. As one of Government Technology's 2021 'Top 25 Doers, Dreamers & Drivers', he is currently focused on the impact of social media from a cyber and kinetic security perspective.

47661.title: Researcher
47661.bio: Karel Dhondt is a researcher whose interests lie in the security and privacy of online location-based services.

44942.title: Postdoctoral Researcher
44942.bio: Victor Le Pochat is a postdoctoral researcher in web security and privacy at the DistriNet research unit of KU Leuven. His research interests lie in exploring large web ecosystems, understanding how to detect and mitigate harmful online content, and both analyzing and improving current research methods. He maintains Tranco, a research-oriented top sites ranking.

47862.title: Scientist
47862.bio: Sara Farmer is a principal technical advisor on DSTL's Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD) program; her other work at DSTL has included cyber hardening for autonomous vehicle systems. Her previous work includes autonomous system design, underwater systems design, and large-scale data science.

49131.title: Founding Partner
49131.bio: David is experienced in the design and implementation of advanced statistical and machine learning techniques. He holds an MA in Mathematics from Cambridge and an MSc in Operational Research.

46960.title: Principal Systems Engineer
46960.bio: James is a Principal Systems Engineer within QinetiQ Training & Simulation. He is currently leading on the development of training and demonstration environments under the ARCD programme

49130.title: Principal Data Scientist
49130.bio: Andy is a Principal Data Scientist within QinetiQ and a Fellow of the Operational Society with over thirty years’ experience of applying data science across multiple domains. He is currently leading on the development of experimentation and evaluation under the ARCD programme

48181.title: Managing Consultant
48181.bio: Ian Miles is a Technical Lead for the mature concepts area of the Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD) research project, which is funded by the UK Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (Dstl) and exploring machine learning automated cyber response and recovery. Ian's previous experience includes MilSatCom, and reliability engineering across UK Defence and industry.

48897.title: Senior Consultant
48897.bio: Matthew is a Fellow of the institute of Engineering and Technology, with over 20 years experience of leading technical teams tasked with complex R&D challenges.  His work has spanned cryptographic network design, digital forensics, advanced radio communications, aviation security and biometrics, as well industrial product innovation.

48923.title: Executive Scientist
48923.bio: Dr. Chris Willis is an Executive Scientist within BAE Systems AI Labs. He has over 25 years’ experience in academia and industry, specializing in the research, development, and application of machine learning and deep learning techniques. Chris is a Chartered Mathematician, and a Fellow of the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications.

48922.title: Data Research Scientist
48922.bio: Dr. Dan Harrold is Senior Research Scientist with extensive RL experience across industry and academia, with publications in high-ranking journals applying RL to real-world problems. He has been the technical lead of a number of Dstl’s Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD)s, developing algorithms designed for Autonomous Cyber Operations and assisting with the development of ARCD environments.

48921.title: Senior Data Scientist
48921.bio: Chris Parry is a Principal Data Scientist with a background in Machine Learning and Software Engineering. Chris has made a number of contributions to Dstl’s Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD) program, including the development of RL agents and environments, and also has experience researching and developing Deep Learning models for other Defence domains, such as Electronic Warfare.

48920.title: Senior Principal Research Scientist
48920.bio: Dr. Gregory Palmer is a Senior Principal Research Scientist within BAE Systems Digital Intelligence, working on autonomous agents and multi-agent systems. He has been the technical lead on a number of projects for DSTL's Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD) program, which have in particular focused on the adversarial learning aspect of the autonomous cyber-defence challenge.

48905.title: Head of Research
48905.bio: John serves as the Head of Research at Trustworthy AI, where he leads TAI's efforts in Cyber Security research with a focus on autonomous decision-making for defensive cyber agents. Prior to joining TAI full-time, John was working towards a PhD in AI and Cyber Security. Earlier in his career, he specialised in offensive security.

48904.title: Mathematical Consultant
48904.bio: Tom Wilson is a Mathematical Consultant at Smith Institute, who holds a PhD in astrophysics from the University of Exeter.  Tom specialises in novel applications of multi-agent cyber defence and optimisation-based strategies. His experience spans machine learning, numerical modelling, and data analysis, with a focus on applications in the defence and energy sectors.

48903.title: CEO / Cofounder
48903.bio: Dr Ryan Heartfield is CEO and co-founder of Exalens, an innovative UK startup developing autonomous cyber-physical detection and response technology for securing operational technology systems. Ryan has over 15 years of experience applying state-of-the-art Intrusion Detection, Network Security, SecOps, and AI for cybersecurity across National Security, Private Sector and Academia

48901.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
48901.bio: Demian Till is a Senior AI Engineer at Cambridge Consultants who has focussed primarily on deep learning-based research projects. His background is in machine learning (MSc University College London) and computer science (MSci University of Glasgow).

48900.title: AI and Algorithms developer
48900.bio: David Rimmer works in AI, data science and algorithm development, including projects applying AI to security problems and AI assurance. He has a background in Bayesian methods and wireless physical layer research, and has contributed to autonomous vehicle research, medical device developments and data-driven system modelling and analysis.

48899.title: Software Engineer
48899.bio: Samuels expertise covers multiple disciplines, with a proven track record in implementing Machine Learning (ML) solutions. He holds an MEng in Computer Science from the University of Warwick, and his contributions include ML architectural analysis and improvement, development of cloud training and deployment pipelines, creation of efficient algorithms, and maintenance of complex software systems managing very large datasets.

48898.title: Principal Machine Learning Engineer
48898.bio: Peter is a Principal Machine Learning Engineer at Cambridge Consultants, with substantial experience in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI), ranging from academic research with the University of St Andrews, though to deployable AI. Peter has a background in Mechanical Engineering, an MSc in AI, and now focuses his work on developing Deep Learning systems, particularly within the Defence and Security sector.

48896.title: Head of AI Engineering
48896.bio: Jack Stone is the AI technical lead for Co-Decyber which is an advanced Cooperative Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning solution for cyber defence, which is part of the Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD) research project, funded by the UK Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (Dstl). Jack’s main focus is on developing reliable AI systems that deliver real world impacts.

48895.title: Cybersecurity specialist
48895.bio: Madeline is an experienced cybersecurity professional with more than 10 years’ experience in a range of sectors including in autonomous systems, computing, IoT, automotive and future mobility. Her technical background encompasses methods for cybersecurity and AI assurance, and she has an extensive track record in leading research and innovation programs, bringing novel ideas from basic technology readiness levels through to technological maturity.

48894.title: Cyber Defence Research Specialist
48894.bio: Pedro is a cyber security researcher working on the development of BT's Inflame tool, focused on malware simulation and threat response, with an emphasis on reinforcement learning techniques. Previously he completed a PhD from City, University of London, on the topic of software reliability for cyber security.

48893.title: Automated Response Research Manager
48893.bio: Alfie Beard is a research manager at BT, leading on automated security response research; currently he leads Inflame, BT’s threat simulation and automated response tool. His research focuses on applying deep reinforcement learning to cybersecurity and through this he contributes to DSTL's Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD) programme.

48892.title: CTO Data & AI, GSS
48892.bio: Jonathan is an expert in applying machine learning and artificial intelligence to exploit data for cyber defence, resilience and intelligence. His research interests include ML/AI, cyber effect, disinformation, privacy and open-source intelligence.

48886.title: Senior Data Scientist
48886.bio: Alec is a Senior Data Scientist specialising in Machine Learning with a particular interest in Reinforcement Learning.

48887.title: Data Scientist/AI Specialist
48887.bio: Ryan is a Data Scientist specialising in applied machine learning research. ORCID

48889.title: Principal Cyber Security Consultant
48889.bio: Principal Cyber Security Consultant (ISC2 CISSP, CCSP; ISACA CISM) with 20+ year experience in cyber security, R&D (at HP Labs), trusted advisory, security software solutions, enterprise, cloud, IT and OT systems. MSc and BSc in AI/ML and computer science. Senior IEEE member with 30+ referred papers published at international conferences and journals. Passionate about applying innovation to address business needs. Named inventor of 50+ USPD patents of which 31 granted.

48888.title: Principal AI Specialist
48888.bio: Principal AI Specialist with over 9 years’ experience in Data Science. PhD in Physical Oceanography, which focussed on modelling the North Atlantic Ocean, a complex system understood through fluid dynamics. ORCID

48891.title: Principal Data Scientist
48891.bio: Lisa Gralewski is the co-lead of BMT's Data AI Team. She is a contributor to the Autonomous Resilient Cyber Defence (ARCD) research project, which is funded by the UK Defence Science & Technology Laboratory (Dstl) and exploring machine learning automated cyber response and recovery. Lisa is an experienced Data Scientist working in the area of cyber security.

48890.title: AI Lead
48890.bio: Senior Principal AI Lead Consultant with over 24 years’ experience in AI research and development in various application domains including Computer Vision, Cyber Security. Dr Turkbeyler holds a range of advisory positions including, board member for MOD AI Strategy Board, board member for Accountable, Responsible, Transparent AI (ART-AI) CDT of Bath University, and executive committee member of IET in Vision and Imaging Network.

32547.title: Founder
32547.bio: Thomas Roth aka stacksmashing is a security researcher mostly focused on hardware and firmware. His work includes hardware attacks on processors, microcontrollers and cryptocurrency wallets, building cheap JTAG tooling for the iPhone, and attacking a wide variety of embedded devices. He also runs a YouTube channel called stacksmashing about security, reverse engineering and hardware hacking.

35799.title: Security Researcher
35799.bio: Martin Doyhenard is a Security Researcher at Portswigger, known for exploiting HTTP servers and web applications. Over the past few years, he has presented his findings in multiple top security conferences including Black Hat, DEFCON, RSA, EkoParty, Hack in The Box and Troopers. His latest work includes discovering HTTP Response Smuggling techniques and exploiting SAP's Inter-Process Communication service - compromising more than 200 thousand companies in the world. He's also passionate about low level reverse engineering and testing his skills in online CTFs.

48221.title: Senior Security Researcher
48221.bio: Adrian Coleșa is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca (TUCN) in Romania, where he has dedicated 26 years of service. He earned his PhD from TUCN and specializes in teaching courses such as Operating Systems (OS), Secure Coding, and Virtualization-Based Security. His primary research focus since 2013 has been in the field of cybersecurity. Additionally, he has been leading a cybersecurity master's program at TUCN since 2015. Since 2019, he has held the position of Senior Security Researcher at Bitdefender, concentrating on virtualization and operating system security. Adrian obtained the OSCP certification in 2014. He has coauthored around 40 scientific papers and six US patents, primarily in cybersecurity.

48223.title: Quantum Software Engineer
48223.bio: Sorin Boloș is a software engineer turned to quantum computing. After earning his stripes in the tech world and diving deep into computer science, he had a fling with quantum computing, thanks to a flirty course by MIT, and it turned into a full-blown love affair. As a proud Qiskit Advocate, he has been spreading the quantum love through talks, courses, and hosting some cool minds. Now, he is on a mission to crack the code on quantum security.

48498.title: PhD Student
48498.bio: Tiejin Chen is a first year Ph.D. student in Computer Science at Arizona State University supervised by Prof. Hua Wei. Prior to this, he obtained a bachelor's degree in statistics from Sichuan University in 2020 and a master's degree in applied statistics from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor in 2023. He specializes in trustworthy machine learning.

45930.title: PhD Student
45930.bio: Wang Zicheng is currently serving as a Research Assistant at the University of Colorado Boulder, he is also pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science at Nanjing University in China. With a deep interest in operating system security, Wang's ongoing research focuses on leveraging the power of eBPF to advance security research in the operating system kernel.

48499.title: Assistant Professor
48499.bio: Hua Wei is an assistant professor at the School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence (SCAI) at Arizona State University (ASU). He got his PhD from Pennsylvania State University in 2020. He specializes in data mining, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. He has been awarded the Best Paper at ECML-PKDD 2020, and has been published in top conferences (NeurlPS, AAAI, KDD, IJCAI, CDC, ECML-PKDD, WWW, CIKM).

39330.title: Assistant Professor
39330.bio: Yueqi Chen is an Assistant Professor at the University of Colorado Boulder. His research interest is system and software security and centers around weird machine concepts. Yueqi desires to understand the weird machine, especially for cyber infrastructures (e.g., Operating Systems, Cryptography Libraries, and Satellite Systems), by developing new exploitation techniques to program weird machines and building protections to anti-program weird machines.

31847.title: CEO
31847.bio: Sherri Davidoff is the CEO of LMG Security and the author of three books, including "Ransomware and Cyber Extortion" and "Data Breaches: Crisis and Opportunity." As a recognized expert in cybersecurity, she has been called a "security badass" by the New York Times. Sherri has been featured as the protagonist in the book, Breaking and Entering: The Extraordinary Story of a Hacker Called "Alien." She is a GIAC-certified forensic examiner (GCFA) and penetration tester (GPEN) and received her degree in Computer Science and Electrical Engineering from MIT.

39528.title: Senior Writer/Editor, Cybersecurity
39528.bio: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai is a Senior Writer at TechCrunch, where he covers hacking, cybersecurity, surveillance, and privacy. Lorenzo is also writing a book about the technology surveillance provider Hacking Team, and the history of government malware.

48799.title: Reporter
48799.bio:
Robert McMillan writes about computer security, hackers and privacy from The Wall Street Journal's San Francisco bureau. Previously, he was a writer at Wired, the IDG News Service and Linux Magazine, where he covered cloud computing, business technology, bitcoin, artificial intelligence and open-source software.

He was the host of Hack Me if You Can, a three-part podcast profile of the Russian hacker Dmitry Smilyanets, produced by the Journal.

48932.title: Partner
48932.bio: Sadia Mirza is a Partner at Troutman Pepper.  Sadia leads the firm's Incidents + Investigations team, advising clients on all aspects of data security and privacy issues. She is the first point of contact when a security incident or data breach is suspected, and plays a central role in her clients' cybersecurity strategies. Sadia's practice is dedicated to counseling clients on complex data security and privacy issues. Capitalizing on her extensive experience guiding clients through security incidents, she handles pre-incident planning and readiness, breach investigations, and litigation matters. Sadia leverages her 360-degree knowledge of the incident response lifecycle to ensure clients can present a positive and defensible narrative to plaintiffs or regulators. Clients also turn to Sadia for best practices related to privacy compliance and novel data-use questions and concerns. An active and respected voice in the privacy and data security bar, she writes and speaks frequently on trends and developments affecting clients and consumers. Sadia has been a panelist on numerous privacy and cybersecurity panels across the U.S. and is a member of the Program Committee for the Law Track for the RSA Conference. Sadia provides ongoing analysis and commentary on developments in the consumer financial services industry, with a focus on privacy law, through the Consumer Financial Services Law Monitor blog at cfslawmonitor.com. She frequently publishes in Bloomberg Law and Law360. Sadia is a Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP/US) and Certified Information Privacy Manager (CIPM).

49031.title: Chief Power Grid Scientist
49031.bio:
Dr. Emma M. Stewart, is a respected power systems and critical infrastructure security specialist with expertise in electric distribution, renewable energy, modeling, and simulation, as well as operational cybersecurity. She holds a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering and an M.Eng. degree in Electrical and Mechanical Engineering. Emma is currently the Chief Power Grid Scientist at Idaho National Labs and the Director of the Center for Securing the Digital Energy Transition. Emma also served as the Chief Scientist at the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association (NRECA), where she led NRECA Research and the Co-Op Cyber Program. Her responsibilities included providing electric cooperatives with education, training, information sharing, incident support, technology integration, and R&D services.

Dr. Stewart's employment history also includes positions at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. At Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, she served as the Associate Program Leader for Cyber and Infrastructure Resilience, managing research on prevention and response to high consequence grid events such as wildfire and cyber-attack. At Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, she was the Deputy Group Leader in the Grid Integration Group and played a major role in developing the first micro-synchrophasor network in the US enabling the data to be used to prevent wildfire and equipment failure.

Throughout her career, Dr. Stewart has made significant contributions to the field of security of power systems, receiving patents for innovations in power distribution systems and data analytics, and truly works at the center of the clean energy, energy security and cybersecurity Venn diagram.

49274.title: Chief Technology Officer
49274.bio:
Nand Mulchandani joined the CIA as Chief Technology Officer in June 2022. In this role, he focuses on driving CIA's efforts in leveraging cutting-edge and future innovations to further CIA's mission. He previously served as the Chief Technology Officer and Acting Director of the U.S. Department of Defense Joint Artificial Intelligence Center (JAIC). Prior to that, he spent 25+ years in the technology industry as a serial entrepreneur and senior executive in the enterprise infrastructure and security software industry as co-founder & CEO of Oblix (acquired by Oracle), Determina (acquired by VMware), OpenDNS (acquired by Cisco), and ScaleXtreme (acquired by Citrix), and as an EIR at the venture capital firm Accel Partners.

Mulchandani holds a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science and Mathematics from Cornell University, a Master of Science in Management from the Stanford University Graduate School of Business, and a Master of Public Administration from the Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University.

49275.title: Director for Strategy
49275.company: White House Office of the National Cyber Director
49275.bio: Lauryn Williams is Director for Strategy in the Office of the National Cyber Director (ONCD), where she drives White House efforts to bolster space system cybersecurity, as well as international cyber policy issues. Lauryn joined ONCD from the Department of Defense, where she served in the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Space Policy and led DoD efforts to better leverage commercial space capabilities and space industry outreach, as well as development of norms of responsible behavior in space. Before DoD, she served in the Department of Energy’s National Nuclear Security Administration and the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Lauryn received her bachelors degree from Stanford University and Masters degree in public and international affairs from Princeton University.

37301.title: Co-Founder and CEO
37301.bio:
Dr. Amit Elazari is the Co-Founder and CEO of OpenPolicy, the world's first tech-enabled and AI powered policy and engagement platform, aiming to democratize access to government affairs and policy.

She teaches at the University of California (UC), Berkeley School of Information Master in Information and Cybersecurity, & RUNI, and serves as a member of the External Advisory Committee for the UC Berkeley Center of Long Term Cybersecurity. Amit is also a public speaker, and often keynotes or speaks at global conferences such as RSA Security, BlackHat, CES, and SXSW.

Prior to OpenPolicy she was Head of Global Cybersecurity Policy at Intel Corporation, responsible for shaping and executing Intel's global security policy and government affairs engagement across all of Intel technologies.

In 2023 she chaired the Cybersecurity Policy Committee for the Information Technology Industry Council, U.S. leading Tech trade association, and the Linux Open Source Security Foundation public policy committee.

Amit holds a Doctoral Degree in the Law (J.S.D.) from UC Berkeley School of Law, the world's leading law institution for technology law, and graduated summa cum laude three prior degrees in law and business.

Her research in tech law and policy has appeared in leading technology law and computer science journals, presented at conferences such as RSA and USENIX Security, and featured at leading news sites such as The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post and the New York Times. You can find her publications on Google Scholar.

35652.title: Security Researcher
35652.bio: Alex Plaskett (@alexjplaskett) is a security researcher within the Exploit Development Group (EDG) at NCC Group. Alex is a five-time Pwn2Own winner (desktop, mobile, embedded, and automotive) and has over 15+ years of experience in vulnerability research and exploitation. Alex has exploited vulnerabilities in a large range of high-profile products across many different areas of security. Alex is a frequent speaker at security conferences (e.g. OffensiveCon, Hexacon, HITB, BlueHat, POC, Troopers, etc). Alex was previously leading security teams in Fintech, Mobile Security and Security Research and just generally causing vendors to patch things on a regular basis!

47702.title: Senior Security Consultant
47702.bio: Robert Herrera (@robert.herrera_) is a Senior Security Consultant within the Hardware/Embedded Security (HES) team at NCC Group. Robert has extensive experience performing security audits for a diverse set of technologies ranging from automotive, modems, secure boot platforms, and reverse-engineering pretty much any firmware that comes his way. Robert has 7+ years of experience and has worn many hats over the years ranging from iOS Developer, Software Engineer, to Reverse Engineer.

41928.title: Security Researcher
41928.bio: Julien Voisin is a security researcher.

42095.title: Sr. Director Security Research
42095.bio: Shachar Menashe is the Senior Director of Security Research at JFrog. With over 15 years of experience in security research, including low-level R&D, reverse engineering and vulnerability research, Shachar is responsible for leading a team of researchers in discovering and analyzing emerging security vulnerabilities and malicious packages. He joined JFrog through the Vdoo acquisition in June 2021, where he served as vice president of security. Before joining Vdoo, Shachar worked as a team leader at boutique research company NorthBit which was acquired by AR giant Magic Leap. He was then put in charge of Magic Leap's low-level OS security team, where he continued specializing in areas such as Linux & Android security architecture, implementing custom kernel and bootloader mitigations, and securing development lifecycle processes. This led to a successful release of Magic Leap's OS which has remained unhacked to this day. Shachar holds a BSc in Electronics Engineering and Computer Science from Tel-Aviv University.

47931.title: Security Researcher
47931.bio: Kazuki Matsuo is a security researcher at FFRI Security specializing in low-level security, who recently graduated with a master's degree from Waseda University this year. He majored in computer science during his undergraduate and graduate studies, focusing on UEFI security. With an intense passion for low-level security, he conducted research on obfuscation of UEFI modules, and won the Student Paper Award at Computer Security Symposium 2022, the largest academic security conference in Japan. He will also present his research at DIMVA 2024. His main interests are negative rings, such as hypervisors, SMM and ME.

47976.title: Director of Transportation, Mobility & Cyber-Physical Systems
47976.bio: Sam Beaumont (PANTH13R) is the Director of Transportation, Mobility, and Cyber-Physical Systems at NetSPI, Sam is at the forefront of developing and delivering technical strategies and solutions for Hardware and Integrated Systems at NetSPI. With a career spanning 10+ years in tech and cybersecurity, Sam has established a formidable reputation for hacking anything with a chip – from hardware and embedded systems to all things that "fly, sail, or drive". Her extensive expertise provides NetSPI customers with unmatched technical leadership, depth, and delivery excellence in advisory and cybersecurity services, ensuring assets existing in physical spaces are fortified against evolving threats. In previous roles, Sam has served in a technical capacity as an offensive security Principal Consultant, Red Teamer, Exploit Developer, Vulnerability Researcher, and more. She has continually demonstrated a unique ability to bridge the gap between business, regulatory needs, and the most prevalent theoretical vulnerabilities. Sam's commitment to the cybersecurity community and approach to tackling cyber-physical systems has cemented her status as a practical thought leader in the field. Through continued research, speaking engagements, and mentorship, Sam is dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what's possible for women in cybersecurity, ensuring a safer, more diverse future for those who wish to secure technologies.

43991.title: Director
43991.bio: Larry is a Director at NetSPI responsible for leading and executing IOT/Embedded Penetration Testing and researching new security techniques to ensure the safety of embedded systems. Larry has a master's degree in mathematics with emphases on Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence from Georgia Southern University. He has worked with several Fortune 250 companies both as an embedded systems engineer and security expert focused on medical devices. He has aided in the design and security of multiple devices in the Automotive, Financial, Medical, Wireless, and Multimedia spectrums, has been published in medical journals, and has spoken at conferences all over the globe. Larry has extensive knowledge of the design of various bare metal and low-level embedded devices.

42838.title: Hacker / Creative Director
42838.bio: Fredrik Alexandersson, better known for his hacker handle STÖK, operates at the crossroads of cybersecurity and creativity. With Swedish roots, STÖK has carved out a distinctive niche as a content creator, ethical hacker, bug bounty hunter, keynote speaker, and cybersecurity advisor. His dedication to uncovering vulnerabilities and enhancing digital security shines through his robust YouTube community, boasting around 130,000 subscribers and over 3 million views by January 2024. His insights have graced the main stages of globally recognized cybersecurity events such as Black Hat USA, DEF CON, Securityfest, SEC-T, Disobey, and Eko Party, further establishing his influence. Diving into cybersecurity in the early '90s, STÖK has pioneered a holistic approach, harmonizing defensive strategies with an aggressive hacker's mindset. However, his expertise extends beyond the digital frontier, incorporating a keen understanding of human psychology, marketing, fashion, and effective communication, reflecting his multifaceted interests and talents. STÖK embodies a lifestyle where technology meets creativity, adopting a positive, forward-thinking stance on security and life. His ethos, captured in the empowering slogan "HACKERS GONNA HACK. CREATORS GONNA CREATE. GOOD VIBES ONLY," strikes a chord with his audience, injecting a vibrant, optimistic outlook into the complex cybersecurity landscape.

48170.title: Head of Security Testing
48170.bio: Joona Hoikkala is a seasoned hacker with over two decades of experience in the fields of software development and information security. He is recognized for his significant contributions to the open-source community, notably his work on acme-dns, ffuf, and certbot. As the creator of ffuf (Fuzz Faster U Fool), a web fuzzing tool, Joona has become a leading figure in the field of web security. ffuf is celebrated for its accuracy, reliability, and speed, and is designed to give users maximum control over their fuzzing processes. It's equipped with a variety of features to cater to different aspects of web security, from resource discovery to password bruteforcing and much more, demonstrating its versatility as a "Swiss army knife" for security professionals. Currently, Joona works as the Head of Security Testing at Visma where he applies his broad range of skills in information security to lead offensive and defensive security testing efforts. His commitment to the security community extends beyond his professional work, as he is an active participant in discussions and developments within the field.

49082.title: Software Engineer, AI Security
49082.bio: Tamir Ishay Sharbat is a Software Engineer in AI Security at Zenity.

48159.title: Research Assistant
48159.bio: Fabian Bäumer completed his M.Sc. degree in IT security by the end of 2021. Since 2022, Fabian has been working as a PhD student at Ruhr University Bochum and is part of the Chair for Network and Data Security. Currently, he is researching the SSH (Secure Shell) network protocol from a security standpoint. As a researcher, Fabian is always on the lookout for interesting research ideas related to (cryptographic) network protocols and "crypto in the wild." You can find Fabian on X, formerly known as Twitter, @TrueSkrillor

48460.title: Independent Researcher
48460.bio: Dyon Goos is an Independent Researcher and holds a Master's degree in Computer Science from the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. He is interested in the security of embedded devices and his main research areas cover fuzzing and reverse engineering cellular baseband stacks. Currently, Dyon is working as an Independent Researcher on analyzing basebands.

37705.title: Assistant Professor
37705.bio: Marius Muench is an assistant professor at the University of Birmingham. His research interests cover (in-)security of embedded systems, binary & microarchitectural exploitation, and defenses. He obtained his PhD from Sorbonne University in cooperation with EURECOM and worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. He developed and maintains avatar2, a framework for analyzing embedded systems firmware, and FirmWire, an emulation and fuzzing platform for cellular basebands. Throughout his career, Marius publicly shared his findings and presented at venues such as Black Hat, REcon, and Hardwear.io.

48906.title: Partner
48906.bio:
Piotr Ciepiela is a cybersecurity and emerging technology expert. He focuses on areas such as OT/IoT, cloud computing, quantum computing, and AI. He is also a professional specializing in critical infrastructure protection for the European Union and national governments. Piotr is a co-author of several international standards for security and emerging technologies.

With 20 years of experience managing international technology projects across the US, Europe, Asia, South America, and the Middle East, his current role is the EY EMEIA Cybersecurity Leader and Global Leader in Security Architecture and Emerging Technologies. He is a co-founder of the Operational Technology (OT) and IoT teams at EY.

Author of a book on critical infrastructure and numerous articles in international magazines, including the Harvard Business Review and Forbes. He participates in the creation of international standards and supports governments in critical infrastructure protection.

Member of the World Economic Forum in the area of resilience. He has been a keynote speaker at global cybersecurity events and is a university lecturer on protection of industrial control systems and management among others at University of Dallas.

49049.title: National Cyber Director
49049.bio:
Harry Coker, Jr. was confirmed by the Senate on December 12, 2023, as the second National Cyber Director in the White House Office of the National Cyber Director. Director Coker is a retired Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) senior executive and career Naval Officer, is a graduate of the US Naval Academy, the Naval Postgraduate School, and Georgetown University Law Center.

Previously, Coker served as Executive Director of the National Security Agency (NSA). Coker's service to the Nation and NSA was recognized with the awarding of the National Intelligence Distinguished Service Medal, the NSA Director's Distinguished Service Medal, and the IC EEOD Outstanding Leadership Award.

During the first seventeen years of his service with the CIA, Coker was assigned to leadership positions in the Directorate of Digital Innovation; the Directorate of Science & Technology; and the Director's Area. Key assignments included service as Director of the Open Source Enterprise, which is responsible for leveraging publicly available information; and as Deputy Director of CIA's Office of Public Affairs. Coker's leadership and contributions earned him the Presidential Rank Award and CIA's prestigious Don Cryer Award for Diversity & Inclusion.

49249.title: Chief Trust Officer
49249.bio:
As Chief Trust Officer, Steve Kelly establishes IST's efforts to advance the trust, safety, and security of artificial intelligence and helps lead other aspects of the organization's work. Steve comes to IST after serving on the National Security Council (NSC) staff as Special Assistant to the President and Senior Director for Cybersecurity and Emerging Technology and retiring from the FBI as a supervisory special agent.

In his White House role, Steve led national policymaking and advised NSC leadership and the President on matters involving cyber defense, critical infrastructure security and resilience, cyber incident management, and relevant emerging technologies. He served as chair of the U.S. government's cyber response group, vulnerabilities equities process, the cyber interagency policy committee, and facilitated the successful launch of the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark security labeling program for consumer technology. He previously served on the NSC staff in 2013-2015, during which time he was instrumental in developing Presidential Policy Directive (PPD) 41 on United States Cyber Incident Coordination.

Steve joined the FBI as a special agent soon after the 9/11 terrorist attacks and served within the Bureau's cyber program for nearly 22 years in various field and headquarters roles. These included cybercrime and cyber/counterintelligence investigations, private sector and international engagement, strategy/policy, and leadership. His last FBI role was as Chief of Cyber Policy.

While in government service, Steve contributed to numerous reports, plans, and policies—many non-public—which include: U.S. National Cybersecurity Strategy (2023); U.S. Government Cyber Deterrence Playbook (2021); World Economic Forum's Partnership Against Cybercrime report (2020); Report of the Cyberspace Solarium Commission (2020); Report of the Attorney General's Cyber-Digital Task Force (2018); U.S. National Cyber Strategy (2017); PPD-41 on United States Cyber Incident Coordination (2016); U.S. Cyber Incident Severity Schema (2015); and the NSTAC's Report to the President on Information and Communications Technology Mobilization (2014).

Prior to his government service, Steve practiced as a registered professional engineer.

43512.title: Research Scientist
43512.bio: Toshinori Usui is a research scientist and security principal at NTT Security Holdings Corporation, with 10+ years of experience in binary analysis, malware analysis, and offensive security. Toshinori has presented his research in top-tier academic conferences such as RAID and ACSAC. He is also a CTF lover focused on reversing and pwn, formerly belonging to Sutegoma2 and binja and currently Team Enu. Toshinori's security interests focus not only on cyber but also on physical, so he usually practices Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu to fight against real-world threats. Toshinori received his Ph.D. in 2021 and has some security certificates, including GREM and GCFE.

44009.title: Senior Researcher
44009.bio: Yuto Otsuki is a security researcher. His research interests are memory analysis, reverse engineering and operating system security. He received his D.Eng. degree from Graduate School of Information Science and Engineering, Ritsumeikan University in Japan. From 2016 to 2019, he was engaged in research of malware analysis and digital forensics at NTT Secure Platform Laboratories. He is now with NTT Security Holdings Corporation and mainly focus on research in vulnerability detection and exploitability analysis.

48735.title: Researcher
48735.bio: Ryo Kubota is a cybersecurity researcher working at NTT Security Holdings Corporation. His research focuses on malware analysis and detection. He has a master's degree in computer science from Kyoto University.

48736.title: Distinguished  Researcher
48736.bio: Yuhei Kawakoya is a Distinguished Researcher at NTT Security Holdings Corporation. Since joining NTT in 2005, he has been engaged in R&D on computer security. His research interests include reverse engineering, malware analysis, and vulnerability discovery.

48737.title: Distinguished Researcher
48737.bio: Dr. Makoto Iwamura is a cybersecurity expert with over two decades of experience in the field. Since joining Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation (NTT) in 2002, he has been instrumental in advancing the company's research and development in areas such as DDoS attack mitigation, security vulnerability exploitation countermeasures, and honeypot systems. Currently serving as a Distinguished Researcher at NTT Security Holdings Corporation, Dr. Iwamura continues to push the boundaries of cybersecurity through cutting-edge research and red team operations. In addition to his technical contributions, Dr. Iwamura is dedicated to cultivating the next generation of cybersecurity professionals.

48738.title: Professor
48738.company: Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo
48738.bio:
Kanta Matsuura received his Ph.D. degree in electronics from the University of Tokyo in 1997. He is currently a Professor at the Institute of Industrial Science at the University of Tokyo. From March 2000 to March 2001, he was a visiting scholar at the University of Cambridge. His research interests include cryptography, computer/network security, and security management such as security economics. He was an Associated Editor of IPSJ Journal (2001-2005) and IEICE Transactions on Communications 
(2005-2008), and won a Distinguished-Service Award from the IEICE Communications Society in 2008. He was Editor-in-Chief of Security Management (2008-2012), and is an Editorial-Board member of Design, Codes, and Cryptography (2010-present), and an Area Editor of the Journal of Cybersecurity (2022-present). He is a fellow of IPSJ. He is a senior member of IEEE, ACM, and IEICE. He is President of JSSM (Japan Society of Security Management) (2021-present).

45940.title: PhD Candidate
45940.company: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
45940.bio: Kaixuan Luo is currently a PhD candidate in the Department of Information Engineering at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. Wing Cheong Lau. His research interests are application security and software security. Part of this work was done during his internship at Samsung Research America.

38511.title: PhD Candidate
38511.company: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
38511.bio: Xianbo Wang is currently a PhD candidate at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, working with Prof. Wing Cheong Lau on application protocol security and mobile security research. He has presented his research at renowned security conferences such as USENIX, NDSS, and Black Hat. He is also a long-time fan of CTFs and bug bounty programs.

45941.title: Director of Security
45941.bio: Adonis Fung is now the Director of Engineering, Security at the NA Bixby Lab of Samsung Research America. Adon's primary goal is to make Samsung Bixby secure by breaking and architecting better systems. He knows one thing: that he knows nothing.

45942.title: Senior Director of Engineering
45942.bio: Julien Lecomte is the Head of Software Engineering & Operations of the North America Bixby Lab, working on the AI Voice Assistant platform for Samsung.

31721.title: Professor
31721.company: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
31721.bio: Wing Cheong Lau is currently a Professor in the Department of Information Engineering and the Director of the Mobile Technologies Centre (MobiTeC) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK). Wing received the B.S.(Eng) degree from The University of Hong Kong and the M.S. and PhD degrees in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Texas at Austin. Before returning to academia, Wing worked in the US industry for a decade: He was a Member of the Technical Staff with the Performance Analysis Department, at Bell Laboratories, Holmdel, New Jersey, where he conducted research in high-speed network protocol design and performance analysis. Wing also had a stint with Qualcomm, San Diego, California where he designed the architecture and protocols for the Next Generation Wireless Packet Data Networks and actively contributed to the standardization of such protocols in the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) and 3GPPs. While on leave from Bell Labs, Wing taught at the University of Hong Kong and served as the Associate Director for the MSc Programme in E-Commerce and Internet Computing. Wing's innovations have led to the granting of 19 U.S. patents. Related research findings have culminated in more than 100 publications in major international conferences and journals. His recent research interests include: Security and Privacy of Online Social Networks and Mobile Payment Systems, Resource allocation and Optimization for Big Data Processing/Cloud Computing Systems, and authenticated 2D barcodes and their applications. Dr. Lau is a Senior Member of IEEE and is a member of ACM and Tau Beta Pi. He is/has been a TPC member of ACM MobiHoc, Sigmetrics, IEEE Infocom, SECON, WiOpt, ICC, Globecom, WCNC, VTC, ITC, VNC and COMSNETS. He also served as a Guest Editor for the special issue on High-speed Network Security of IEEE Journal of Selected Areas in Communications (JSAC). For their work in Single-Sign-On SDK security, Wing and his team received the 2018 Internet Defense Prize (2nd-runner up) from Usenix and Facebook.

37664.title: Senior Research Scientist
37664.bio: Dhilung Kirat is a Senior Research Scientist in the AI Supply Chain Security group at IBM T.J. Watson Research Center. Dhilung received his PhD in Computer Science from the University of California, Santa Barbara. His research interests revolve around areas of computer security, in particular malware analysis, AI-powered security analytics, and ethical hacking research. You can follow Dhilung on X @dhilung

37837.title: Principal Research Scientist
37837.bio: Jiyong Jang is a Principal Research Scientist and Manager of the AI Supply Chain Security team at the IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center. He completed his Ph.D. degree at Carnegie Mellon University. His research interests include most areas of computer security, with an emphasis on software and network security. His current research focuses on security analytics to detect advanced threats in complex networking systems, and application security to identify and remediate vulnerabilities using static and dynamic analysis.

48151.title: Security Researcher
48151.bio: Vlad Babkin is currently a Security Researcher at Eclypsium with over 10 years of experience in networking, security, firmware research and software engineering. He is a long-time member of dcua CTF team and is passionate about breaking software and firmware to make the world a safer place.

35248.title: Principal Security Researcher
35248.bio: Orange Tsai, is the principal security researcher of DEVCORE and the core member of CHROOT security group in Taiwan. He is also the champion and the "Master of Pwn" title holder in Pwn2Own 2021 and 2022. In addition, Orange has spoken at several top conferences such as Black Hat USA (5 times), DEF CON (5 times), HITCON (11 times), CODE BLUE (6 times), POC, Hexacon, HITB GSEC/AMS, and WooYun! Currently, Orange is a 0day researcher focusing on web/application security. His research not only earned him the Pwnie Awards winner for "Best Server-Side Bug" in 2019 and 2021 but also secured 1st place in the "Top 10 Web Hacking Techniques" for 2017 and 2018. In his free time, Orange also engages in bug bounties. He is especially enthusiastic about RCE, successfully identifying critical RCEs across a broad range of vendors, including Twitter, Facebook, Uber, Apple, Netflix, Tesla, GitHub, Amazon, and more. You can follow Orange on X @orange_8361 and https://blog.orange.tw/

32938.title: Ceo/Cofounder
32938.bio: Patrick Wardle is the CEO and Cofounder of DoubleYou, the founder of the non-profit Objective-See Foundation, and the author of "The Art of Mac Malware" book series. Having worked at NASA and the NSA, as well as presenting at countless security conferences, he is intimately familiar with aliens, spies, and talking nerdy. Passionate about macOS security, Patrick spends his days discovering Apple 0days, studying macOS malware, and releasing free open-source security tools to protect Mac users.

46067.title: Principal Adversary Emulation Engineer
46067.bio: Michael Kouremetis is a Principal Adversary Emulation Engineer and the MITRE Caldera™ project lead at the MITRE Corporation. Michael focuses on applying artificial intelligence, data science and software engineering to the cyber domain. Previously, Michael has worked at Boeing and for the intelligence community. Michael has computer science degrees from Purdue and Embry-Riddle, and is currently pursuing a degree in artificial intelligence at Johns Hopkins. Michael is an avid reader, motorcycle rider, and aspiring pickle ball phenom.

48440.title: Senior Artificial Intelligence Engineer
48440.bio: Marissa Dotter is a Senior Artificial Intelligence Engineer at the MITRE Corporation. Marissa primarily focuses on AI Assurance and Security through developing and maintaining the MITRE ATLAS™ framework as well as developing tools within Caldera for red team emulation on AI-enabled systems. Her previous background has been applying AI/ML to various domains including underwater acoustics, wildfire mitigation, and healthcare. Marissa has Electrical Engineering and Physics degrees from Point Loma Nazarene University. Marissa spends as much time as she can outside through gardening, trail running, and reading.

48446.title: Applied Cybersecurity Engineer
48446.bio: Alex Byrne is a Cybersecurity Engineer at MITRE with experience in ethical hacking, machine learning, autonomous systems, and applied mathematics. At MITRE Alex works on multiple R&D projects that sit at the intersection of cyber security and artificial intelligence. Alex has a computer science degree from Florida International University, where he was also an active undergraduate researcher. In his free time, Alex does bass playing, classical and digital art, motorcycle riding, literature, and running.

48650.title: Senior Offensive Security Engineer
48650.bio: Dan Martin is an offensive security expert dedicated to breaking into networks before the bad guys can. Dan is currently pursing a Masters of Science in Information Security Engineering from SANS Technology Institute.

48651.title: Cybersecurity Engineer
48651.bio: Ethan Michalak is a cybersecurity engineer and an avid CTF player.  Ethan pursues efforts in adversary emulation, detection engineering, and malware development.  In his free time, Ethan plays video games, reads a book, or makes a cocktail.

34404.title: Principal Engineer
34404.bio: Gianpaolo Russo is a Principal Engineer and the Capability Area Lead for Autonomous Cyber Operations at the MITRE Corporation. Gianpaolo focuses on building the technical foundations for applying artificial intelligence to cyber operations and developing the roadmap to next-generation autonomous cyber operations within MITRE and across the public sector. Previously, Gianpaolo was a multidisciplinary researcher at Indiana University Bloomington, leading cyber effects research by day, and contributing to cyber policy think tanks by night. Gianpaolo has a Juris Doctor as well as a master’s degree in cyber engineering from Indiana University, and studied Cognitive Science at the University of California, Irvine.

48755.title: Principal AI Research Engineer
48755.bio: Michael Threet is an AI Research Engineer with a background in AI, Generative AI, and AI Infrastructure. He holds a BS and MS in Electrical Engineering from the University of California San Diego. With a strong foundation in electrical engineering, Michael has a deep understanding of the underlying technologies that power AI systems. His educational background has equipped him with the knowledge and skills to design, develop, and optimize AI models, policy, and infrastructure. Recent work includes research at the intersection of Cyber and AI, MITRE's AI Platform for internal virtualized AI infrastructure, and AI Policy for NTIA's response to the Executive Order on AI.

31880.title: Founder
31880.bio: Thomas Brandstetter is a recognized OT cybersecurity expert, with more than 20 years of background in the industry. He is currently active as co-founder and managing director of Limes Security, a major European OT cyber security company. He also is Professor for IT Security at University of Applied Sciences, St. Poelten and Honorary Professor for Cyber Security at DeMontfort University. His past career track record includes being the Stuxnet incident handler for Siemens and founding the Siemens ProductCERT. He often is a keynote and invited guest speaker on the topic of OT and critical infrastructure security. He co-founded and still supports many security community events and initiatives such as the ICS Village at DEFCON/BruCON, IT-SECX and ICS-CSR.

49037.title: Vice President, Supply Chain Security
49037.bio:
Cassie Crossley, Vice President, Supply Chain Security in the global Cybersecurity & Product Security Office at Schneider Electric, is an experienced cybersecurity technology executive in Information Technology and Product Development and author of "Software Supply Chain Security: Securing the End-to-End Supply Chain for Software, Firmware, and Hardware." She has many years of business and technical leadership experience in supply chain security, cybersecurity, product/application security, software/firmware development, program management, and data privacy.

Cassie has designed frameworks and operating models for end-to-end security in software development lifecycles, third party risk management, cybersecurity governance, and cybersecurity initiatives. She is a member of the CISA SBOM working groups and presents frequently on the topic of SBOMs and Supply Chain Security.

Cassie has held previous positions at Ceridian, Hewlett-Packard, McAfee, Lotus, and IBM. She has an M.B.A. from California State University, Fresno, and her Bachelor of Science degree in Technical and Professional Communication with a specialization in Computer Science.

43798.title: CTO and Co-Founder
43798.bio: Mark Carney is a mathematician and hacker working at the intersection of quantum technologies, AI, cybersecurity, music, and more. Currently, Carney is a Co-founder and CTO at Quantum Village, taking place for its third year at DEF CON 32. He holds a PhD in pure mathematics, and has produced ground-breaking work for some time, most recently working on open source tools for cryptography discovery using CodeQL source code analysis (released at BHEU 2023) and CryptoMon, a passive network monitoring.

39522.title: Principal Cryptographer and Global Lead in Quantum Security
39522.bio: Dr. Tommaso Gagliardoni is a mathematician, cryptographer, and quantum security expert. Tommaso published influential peer-reviewed papers in the areas of cryptography, quantum computing, security, and privacy, and spoke at conferences such as CRYPTO, EUROCRYPT, ASIACRYPT, and Black Hat Europe. He is known, among other achievements, for his collaborations in solving the longstanding problem of adaptive quantum authentication (EUROCRYPT 2018, TQC 2019) and breaking the security of ISO-standard smart card protocol PLAID (Real World Crypto 2015, SSR 2015). As a subject expert on quantum security, he serves in the program committee of academic conferences, and collaborates with the WEF, NIST and other official agencies in the context of international agreements and standardization. Expert in blockchain and DeFi technologies, he has performed cryptographic code audits for clients such as Binance, Coinbase, Swiss Post. He also has a background in privacy hacktivism, investigative journalism, and ethical hacking, speaking at venues such as the International Journalism Festival. Tommaso worked at IBM Research before joining the research team of Swiss-American cybersecurity company Kudelski Security, where he is currently technical leader for the initiatives in advanced cryptography services and quantum security.

32328.title: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
32328.bio:
Stephanie Domas started her career with over 10 years of ethical hacking, reverse engineering, and advanced vulnerability analysis as a defense contractor and has a deep knowledge and passion for the hacker mindset.

Pivoting her offensive skills to the defense she built and led two successful cybersecurity businesses focused on defense of embedded systems, medical devices and the healthcare industry.

Stephanie is currently the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) at Canonical, the maintainers of the world's most popular Linux operating system, Ubuntu. Previously she was the Security Technology Strategist for Intel (Fortune 50), where she owned the cross Intel security technology strategy, formulating and implementing strategies that helped accelerate Intel's strength, competitiveness, and revenue growth in the area of Security.

Stephanie is a passionate educator, strategist, speaker, advisor, and security enthusiast.

47587.title: Ph.D. Student
47587.bio: Juhee Kim is a Ph.D. student at CompSec Lab, Seoul National University, advised by Byoungyoung Lee. Her research focuses on both attacks and defenses against software systems, including operating systems and web browsers. Recent studies have centered on security techniques utilizing hardware features, such as ARM's Pointer Authentication Code (PAC) and Memory Tagging Extensions (MTE).

36741.title: Samsung Research
36741.bio: Jinbum Park is a security researcher, working for the Security and Privacy Team at Samsung Research. He is mainly working as a blue team member but has a huge interest in offensive techniques. His main research interests cover from system security to machine learning security. He currently spends most time on Islet project (https://github.com/islet-project/islet), which aims to bring ARM CCA (a new confidential computing hardware primitive) into mobile devices.

48589.title: Seoul National University
48589.bio: Sihyeon Roh is a Ph.D student at CompSec Lab, Seoul National University, and is advised by Byoungyoung Lee. His research focuses on software and hardware vulnerabilities.

48593.title: Seoul National University
48593.bio: Jaeyoung Chung is a Ph.D student at CompSec Lab, Seoul National University, and is advised by Byoungyoung Lee. He is interested in general system security, including bug discovery, attack, and mitigation on kernel and hypervisor.

48590.title: Seoul National University
48590.bio: YoungJoo Lee is a PhD student at Seoul National University, specializing in system security. His research focuses on fuzzing and program analysis, with a particular emphasis on modern web browsers. As a result, he has received bounty rewards from Google VRP for finding vulnerabilities in the Chrome Browser. Additionally, he is an enthusiastic CTF player, concentrating on binary exploitation, and plays as WreckTheLine and CodeRed.

34281.title: Samsung Research and Georgia Institute of Technology
34281.bio: Taesoo Kim is a Professor in the School of Cybersecurity and Privacy and the School of Computer Science at Georgia Tech. He also serves as a director of the Georgia Tech Systems Software and Security Center (GTS3). Starting from his sabbatical year, he works as a VP at Samsung Research, leading the development of a Rust-based OS for a secure element. He is a recipient of various awards including NSF CAREER (2018), Internet Defense Prize (2015), and several best paper awards including USENIX Security'18 and EuroSys'17. He holds a BS from KAIST (2009), a SM (2011) and a PhD (2014) from MIT.

31697.title: Seoul National University
31697.bio: Byoungyoung Lee is an Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Seoul National University (SNU). He is interested in general computer security and privacy-related problems in general. His research focus is systems security, namely attack mitigation, vulnerability finding, and confidential computing.

42281.title: Professor; CEO
42281.bio: Yajin (Andy) Zhou is a professor at Zhejiang University. Yajin earned a Ph.D. (2015) in Computer Science from North Carolina State University and then worked as a senior security researcher at Qihoo 360. Yajin is a co-founder of BlockSec, a startup committed to building blockchain security infrastructure. Yajin has published more than 50 papers, with 9500+ citations (Google Scholar). Two of the papers have been selected to the list of normalized Top-100 security papers since 1981. Yajin was recognized as the Most Influential Scholar Award for contributions to the field of Security and Privacy. Yajin's current research spans traditional ones (software security, operating systems security and hardware-assisted security) and emerging areas (security of smart contracts, decentralized finance (DeFi) security, and underground economy.)

47687.title: Senior Security Researcher
47687.bio: Wang Hongfei is a senior researcher in threat hunting and analysis automation at DBAPPSecurity Research Institute. Wang has been engaged in information security research for more than 5 years and has work experience in many fields such as intrusion detection, emergency response, tool development, and advanced threat discovery and tracking. Wang is currently responsible for the advanced threat detection and discovery research work of DBAPPSecurity. Wang has extensive experience in tracking and discovering APTs. He has tracked multiple APT groups for a long time and independently discovered 3 undisclosed APTs. He has participated in incident response investigations of multiple APT groups such as Lazarus, Bitter, Oceanlotus, APT29, and Sidewinder, etc.

47885.title: Security Research Expert
47885.bio: Wu Dong is a senior expert in advanced threat analysis at DBAPPSecurity Research Institute. Wu has been engaged in information security research for more than ten years and has mature experience in APT attack detection, vulnerability mining and other directions. Wu is currently responsible for the advanced threat detection and discovery research work of DBAPPSecurity. Wu has rich experience in front-end and back-end work, and has accumulated experience in APT technical analysis and vulnerability mining. He independently mined and obtained more than 70 CVE vulnerability numbers. He led the team to discover and first disclosed 9 unknown APT groups and multiple black market gangs and has experience in multiple processes such as product design and development, product management, product operation and promotion, etc.

48952.title: Senior Security Researcher
48952.bio: Gu Yuan is a senior security researcher at DBAPPSecurity with a background in cybersecurity extending over 5 years. She has worked in Reverse Engineering training, and later focused on the discovery of Advanced Persistent Threats, independently discovering multiple unknown APT organizations. Additionally, she continues to track more than 20 APT organizations around the world and has published over 30 public research reports. She has extensive experience in threat hunting and intrusion detection.

47906.title: Red Team & Security Researcher
47906.bio: Yehuda Smirnov is a cybersecurity professional with a focus on Red Teaming, Security Research and Penetration Testing. Yehuda is a dedicated self-learner, always eager to take on new challenges and expand technical expertise.

47978.title: CEO
47978.bio: Narayana Pappu started in Data Science at Fannie Mae before the term existed. He was tasked to build a better home price index than what was available in the market. For 15 years after that at PayPal, Coinbase, and Doctor on Demand, he built and scaled low-latency and high-volume internal investigation, graph, and entity resolution tools for risk management and compliance. He also launched consumer/merchant lending solutions in the US, UK, and Germany with over 5 billion dollars in annual transaction volumes each and drove projects around data monetization with partnerships between PayPal, advertising, and payment networks.  His expertise lies in building complex data solutions that are easy to implement, use, and generate incremental value.

32969.title: VP of Research
32969.bio: Eyal Paz is the VP of Research at OX Security, a software supply chain security leader. His work includes hands-on security research toward a holistic DevSecOps solution. Before joining OX Security, Eyal spent eleven years at Check Point working on security research for product innovation in application security, malware analysis, and phishing prevention. Eyal is also a sought-after university lecturer on various cybersecurity topics. He has a bachelor's degree in Software Engineering and a master's degree in Computer Science. Currently, he is a Ph.D. candidate researching the problem of encrypted traffic classification.

48754.title: Data Scientist and Security Researcher
48754.bio: Liad is a data scientist and security researcher at OX Security. His day-to-day work involves empowering open-source security with AI capabilities. He is passionate about solving complex problems with data-driven approaches. Liad started his career as a young "script kiddie", later becoming a gifted mathematician. Liad holds a Master of Science degree in computer science

32673.title: Assistant Professor
32673.bio: Jianjun Chen's research focuses on studying real-world systems to understand their security challenges, such as security issues in CDN, HTTP implementations, web browsers, and email systems. His previous research has been recognized by top-tier academic security conferences (e.g., NDSS, ACM CCS, USENIX Security) and led to some real-world security pushes, such as patches in popular HTTP implementations (e.g., Squid, Chrome, Firefox ), security advisories by industrial companies (e.g., Akamai, Cloudflare, Apple), web standard change, and a new IETF RFC (RFC 8586).

45697.title: Ph.D. Candidate
45697.bio: Run Guo is a passionate security researcher in the field of information security, with interests focused on offensive network security.

38597.title: Tenured Associate Professor
38597.bio: Chao Zhang is a tenured Associate Professor at the Institute for Network Science and Cyberspace of Tsinghua University. Chao's research covers a range of topics in software security, program analysis, AI security,  and data security. Chao was awarded the following: 2016 DARPA Cyber Grand Challenge CFE (2nd in exploiting), 2015 DARPA Cyber Grand Challenge CQE (1st in defense), 2017 5th place in Defcon CTF, 2016 2nd place in Defcon CTF and 2015 5th place in Defcon CTF.

34453.title: Professor
34453.company: Tsinghua University; Zhongguancun Laboratory; QI-ANXIN Technology Research Institute
34453.bio: Dr. Haixin Duan is a professor of the Institute for Network Sciences and Cyberspace, Tsinghua University. He was once a visiting scholar at UC Berkeley and a senior scientist at the International Computer Science Institute (ICSI) in Berkeley, CA. Prof. Duan has been working on network security for about 30 years. His recent research interests include network protocol security, intrusion detection, underground economy detection and Internet Governance. Many of his research papers have been published by top security or network conferences like IEEE Symposium on Security & Privacy, USENIX Security, ACM CCS, NDSS, SIGCOMM and IMC. He received several best paper or distinguished paper awards from top security conferences including CCS, NDSS and DSN. Some of his research results were deployed in some big IT companies like Baidu, Huawei and Qi-An-Xin Group.

48307.title: Graduate Student
48307.bio: Jiayi Hu is a graduate of Sichuan University and is a graduate student at Zhejiang University. He is a member of the 0x401 CTF team and r3kapig CTF team. His research interest lies in system security, especially Linux kernel security.

48373.title: PhD Student
48373.bio: Jinmeng Zhou is currently working toward the Ph.D. degree in the Department of Computer Science, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang, China. She received the B.S. degree in information security from Wuhan University in 2019. Her research interests include OS kernel security and static program analysis.

48378.title: Undergraduate
48378.bio: Qi Tang is an undergraduate at Jilin University. He is interested in OS security, especially the Linux Kernel. He plays CTF a lot, as an active member of Nu1L Team, and won the Aliyun CTF champion, DEFCON 31 5th place.

45838.title: Professor
45838.bio: Wenbo Shen is currently a ZJU 100-Young Professor at Zhejiang University, China. He received the Ph.D. degree from the Computer Science Department of North Carolina State University in 2015. His research interests are system security and software security, including container security, OS kernel security, and program analysis using LLVM/clang.

45556.title: PHD Student
45556.bio: Niklas Vogel is a routing security researcher at Goethe University Frankfurt. His research is targeted towards the security of Internet Protocols, with a focus on BGP, RPKI, and DNS.

44642.title: Security Researcher
44642.bio: Donika Mirdita is a security researcher at ATHENE, the German National Research Center for Applied Cybersecurity, and a PhD Candidate at the Technical University of Darmstadt. Her research area is network and routing security, with a focus on RPKI, BGP and DNS protocols. Her research results have been published in security conferences such as Usenix, ACM CCS, NDSS and SIGCOMM.

38151.title: Professor
38151.bio: Haya Schulmann is a professor of Cybersecurity at Goethe University Frankfurt.

44275.title: Professor
44275.company: Technical University Darmstadt, Fraunhofer SIT, ATHENE
44275.bio: Michael Waidner is the Director of the Fraunhofer Institute for Secure Information Technology (Fraunhofer SIT) and Professor (Chair) for Security in IT at Technische Universität Darmstadt. He is also the CEO of the National Research Center for Applied Cyber Security ATHENE. Since 2017 he is also the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) of the city of Darmstadt. With more than 130 publications, Michael Waidner is one of the preeminent scientists in IT security. He is an IEEE Fellow and ACM Distinguished Scientist. He received his PhD from the University of Karlsruhe (now known as KIT). Until 2010, he was an IBM Distinguished Engineer and the Chief Technology Officer for Security, responsible for the technical security strategy and architecture of the IBM Corporation. Before that, he headed security research at IBM Zurich Research Laboratory in Rüschlikon, Switzerland.

34820.title: Professor, Dipartimento Di Elettronica, Informazione E Bioingegneria
34820.bio: Stefano Zanero received a PhD in Computer Engineering from Politecnico di Milano, where he is currently a professor with the Dipartimento di Elettronica, Informazione e Bioingegneria. His research focuses on malware analysis, cyberphysical security, and cybersecurity in general. Besides teaching "Computer Security" and "Digital Forensics and Cybercrime" at Politecnico, he has an extensive speaking and training experience in Italy and abroad. He co-authored over 100 scientific papers and books. He is a Senior Member of the IEEE and of the Computer Society, which has named him a Distinguished Visitor and Distinguished Contributor; he is a lifetime senior member of the ACM, which has named him a Distinguished Speaker; and has been named a Fellow of the ISSA (Information System Security Association). Stefano also co-founded Secure Network, a leading cybersecurity assessment firm, and BankSealer, a startup in the FinTech sector that addresses fraud detection through machine learning techniques.
